chapters.title: Chapter 151: Luke Fifth Wife, Elaria
paragraphs: "It contains recent news regarding... Her Highness’s husband."
"Hmm." Haldir’s gaze remained fixed on the newspaper.
Seconds passed.
Then another.
He said nothing.
That silence only made Lyra more nervous.
Tiny beads of sweat gradually appeared across her forehead.
She knew exactly what kind of person Prince Haldir was.
He had punished her on more than one occasion.
Sometimes for reasons she never even understood.
Fortunately.
Princess Elaria had always treated her kindly.
Which was precisely why.
The moment Lyra learned about Luke’s achievements.
Her first thought had been to share the happy news with the princess.
Surely she would be delighted to hear about her husband.
But now watching Prince Haldir silently stare at the newspaper.
Hope slowly faded from her heart.
’It seems impossible.’
’I won’t be able to deliver it to Her Highness...’
The thought left her feeling helpless.
Still she carefully raised her eyes.
Prince Haldir remained standing exactly where he was. Lost in thought.
The newspaper still held his attention.
Lyra quietly lowered her gaze once more.
Although she couldn’t claim to know everything about the royal family.
She had heard countless stories while serving within the palace.
Royal elves viewed themselves as the purest race in existence.
They looked down upon nearly every other race.
Humans, Beastkin, Dwarves.
Even other elves lacking royal blood.
Yet among all of them, the race they despised the most. Was humanity.
The reason was simple.
Throughout history countless elves had been captured and sold as slaves across various continents.
And among all races, humans were the worst offenders.
Unlike others, who conducted such trades in secret. The Human Continent practiced it openly.
Its slave markets also held the largest number of elven captives in the entire world.
Renowned for their unparalleled beauty, elves were considered the most valuable slaves.
Many human nobles, Merchant families, Even members of the imperial household.
Kept elven slaves within their residences.
Naturally The Elven Empire demanded that the Human Empire abolish the practice immediately.
However The Human Emperor at the time ignored every warning.
To him profit and political influence mattered far more than the dignity of another race.
As a result the already strained relationship between humans and elves rapidly deteriorated.
Border disputes became increasingly common.
Skirmishes erupted one after another.
Eventually war became inevitable.
And then the final spark arrived.
An Elven Princess disappeared while traveling to another continent on an official diplomatic mission.
The entire Elven Empire was thrown into chaos.
For elves, the royal family was more than mere rulers.
They were regarded as the direct descendants and guardians of the World Tree itself.
To harm a royal, was equivalent to insulting their god.
An unforgivable sin.
So the empire mobilized every available force.
Days of relentless searching followed.
Finally...
They discovered the truth.
The mastermind behind the kidnapping. Was the Human Emperor himself.
The princess had been imprisoned inside the Imperial Palace.
The moment that truth became known The Elven Empire erupted.
Every army marched, Every noble answered the call.
War was declared without hesitation.
And that war shook the entire world.
Millions perished upon the battlefield.
Countless legendary experts fell.
Kingdoms caught between the two empires were reduced to ruins.
Even neutral races suffered enormous losses.
Many races condemned the Human Emperor for his actions.
Yet his pride never wavered.
He refused every attempt at negotiation. So the war continued.
Until...
The number of casualties reached into the billions.
At last The Elven Demigod awakened.
The protector who had slumbered beneath the World Tree for ages.
With overwhelming power. The demigod descended upon the Human Empire.
Half of the Human Continent was devastated.
The Human Emperor was personally executed.
And the imprisoned Elven Princess was finally rescued.
That single event shook every race across Valtharion.
People suddenly remembered something they had nearly forgotten.
Demigods still existed.
They simply chose not to interfere in mortal affairs.
Most spent their endless lives asleep.
Others wandered the world without concern for kingdoms or wars.
Because of their silence... Many races had gradually forgotten the terror such beings represented.
Although countless races pitied the ordinary humans caught in the catastrophe...
None defended the Human Emperor.
After all the disaster had begun because of his own greed.
At that time humanity was still one of the newest overlord races upon Valtharion.
Unlike dragons, Elves. Or vampires.
Humans possessed neither ancient bloodlines nor a long history.
For thousands of years. Not a single human had successfully reached the Demigod realm.
Only much later did the truth behind the Human Emperor’s obsession come to light.
He hadn’t merely coveted the beauty of other races.
He had been desperately searching for a way to create humanity’s first Demigod.
His plan was to produce descendants carrying the powerful bloodlines of their ancient races.
If humans lacked ancient lineage. Then he would simply steal it.
One experiment after another ended in failure.
Eventually his attention turned toward royal bloodlines.
Especially the elves. Unfortunately for him.
Before his ambition could bear fruit.
The Elven Demigod ended both his life and his dream.
From that day onward, humanity’s position among the overlord races weakened considerably.
Meanwhile...
The elves gradually restored their former glory beneath the protection of the World Tree.
Although, that tragedy had occurred tens of thousands of years ago.
Their hatred towards human never truly faded.
Elves possessed extraordinarily long lifespans.
Many who had personally witnessed that war. Were still alive today. They remembered every battle.
Every death, humiliation and even the princess who had been kidnapped and abused had survived.
And she eventually rose to become one of the strongest elves in existence.
A being standing at the peak of Valtharion. Second only to the Demigods themselves.
"I’ll deliver this to Elaria, you may return to your duties."
Haldir’s voice suddenly interrupted Lyra’s thoughts.
"H-Huh?" Startled, Lyra blinked several times before finally realizing what had happened.
The newspaper was no longer in her hands. Prince Haldir had already taken it.
By the time she looked up. He was calmly walking toward Princess Elaria’s chambers.
’Did I misunderstand him?’ Confusion filled Lyra’s face.

chapters.title: Chapter 152: Why Elaria Become Luke Bride.
paragraphs: After standing there for a moment. She simply shook her head.
There was little point dwelling on it. Quietly, she turned around and returned to her duties.
Meanwhile...
Haldir continued walking through the palace corridors with an expressionless face.
However, inside the sleeve of his royal robe, his hand slowly crushed the newspaper.
The paper crumpled into a ball and the next instant.
A strand of emerald aether silently emerged. Without leaving behind even a single fragment. The newspaper turned to dust.
"Hmph." A cold snort escaped his lips.
"A mere low-born human. actually believes he is worthy of my sister."
"What a laughable dream." His emerald eyes narrowed with unconcealed disgust as he continued toward Elaria’s chamber.
To Haldir, none of that mattered.
It didn’t matter that Luke had awakened astonishing talent.
It didn’t matter that he had reached the Early Bronze Knight realm in such a short time.
Nor did it matter that he had crossed two major realms and effortlessly slain a Mid-Golden Knight.
In Haldir’s eyes, Luke was still nothing more than a human.
"Even the strongest Hero has bowed before the Elven Royal Family."
"And he actually believes he’s worthy of marrying my sister?"
Disgust filled his voice.
Ironically, his words weren’t entirely false.
Although every Hero was summoned from another world and blessed by Valtharion itself.
Not every Hero was equal. Regardless of gender.
Their personalities, determination, and achievements depended entirely upon themselves.
The blessing granted them extraordinary potential.
But, potential alone did not guarantee strength.
Throughout history, countless Heroes had risen. Some reached the pinnacle of the world. Others barely left their names behind.
Haldir himself had already crossed swords with several ancient Heroes.
Only a handful had possessed the qualifications to fight him on equal footing.
The rest, could not even withstand his full strength.
As for Heroes marrying into the Elven Royal Family, that had happened before.
However, whenever the elves turn arrived. The summoned Hero had always been female.
To the elves, it meant that an exceptionally talented Heroine entered their royal family.
Something they had long accepted.
Never before, had a male human Hero been chosen to marry an elven princess.
So when Luke appeared, and the Goddess herself decreed,
The entire kingdom was thrown into confusion.
According to ancient tradition. Only royal blood could marry a Hero.
Naturally, none of the royal families wished to sacrifice one of their own daughters.
Eventually, every gaze turned toward a single person. One of the strongest elves alive.
The legendary princess once kidnapped by the Human Emperor.
During her captivity, the emperor had repeatedly attempted to produce descendants carrying both human and royal elven blood.
Every attempt failed. Although she was rescued,
The ordeal left behind deep emotional scars.
From that day onward. She rejected every proposal and never married.
Nor did she allow any man to approach her.
Then, four hundred and ninety-nine years before Luke’s summoning.
Something impossible happened. Without warning, news spread among Royal Elves, that she had given birth to a child.
A half-elf.
The announcement stunned them. As no one understood how it had happened.
For tens of thousands of years. Nothing.
Then suddenly. One day her abdomen swelled.
And the very next day. Elaria was born.
Among elves, pregnancy normally lasted between two and four years.
This phenomenon defied every known knowledge.
Even today, tts true cause remained a mystery.
Despite everything, she accepted Elaria as her daughter.
And without hesitation. She publicly announced the birth of a royal child.
The Council of Elders was furious. In their eyes. A half-elf threatened the purity of the royal bloodline.
However. No one dared openly oppose her.
Because her strength alone was enough to silence every objection.
Thus the matter was quietly accepted.
When the outside world learned of Elaria’s birth. They were equally bewildered.
Had the legendary princess secretly married? Had she fallen in love?
Countless rumors emerged. Yet...
No answers ever came.
No one connected Elaria’s birth to the Human Emperor.
After all more than ten thousand years had passed since that tragedy. Such an idea seemed absurd.
Then came Luke.
When discussions began regarding which princess should marry the newly summoned Hero.
The council reached a unanimous decision.
*Elaria.*
On this her mother immediately opposed it. She despised humans more than anyone.
And now asking her daughter to marry one. Was simply unacceptable.
Unfortunately this time the Council refused to compromise.
Previously they had tolerated Elaria’s existence because of her mother’s overwhelming strength.
But allowing another generation of mixed royal blood. Especially through a human.
Was a matter they wished to control themselves.
After hundreds of arguments. The Council and the Elders made the final decision.
Even Elaria’s mother could not overturn it.
There was another reason as well. One known only to the royal family.
Although ordinary citizens respected Elaria as a princess. Many royal relatives quietly discriminated against her because she was only half-elven.
Which was why, the other princess would raise questions. That why would a mixed blood didn’t get married to another human, as she was already half human.
So Elaria’s mother reluctantly
Thus when news spread that she had accepted marriage to a human Hero.
And worse a Hero publicly labeled talentless.
The entire world become shocked.
Even so no one dared question her mother directly.
Not after witnessing her strength.
Haldir slowly emerged from his thoughts.
Although Elaria was merely his stepsister. He had watched her grow up.
To him, she was still family.
Which was why he had never accepted her marriage to Luke.
After staring silently toward her residence for a moment.
He quietly turned around. "...No need to disturb her."
With those words. He returned to his own chambers.
While Elaria remained Completely unaware, secluded inside her room.
So she didn’t hear a single word about her husband’s recent achievements.
Meanwhile...
Luke’s name spread across every corner of Valtharion.
Naturally the news reached the ears of the current generation of Heroes.
Most simply glanced at the report before tossing it aside. They didn’t care.
A few male Heroes, however couldn’t hide their jealousy.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: The Saintess’s Wrath | Annihilate Them
paragraphs: After all Luke had somehow married five princesses.
Meanwhile most of them had only one wife.
Still none of them truly regarded Luke as a rival.
Even though an old saying claimed that the last summoned Hero would always become the strongest.
Most of the current Heroes had already reached the peak of the Silver Knight realm.
Many were preparing to break through into the Golden Knight stage.
Compared to them. Luke still seemed far behind.
Even the surviving Heroes from previous generations heard the news.
They merely acknowledged it before returning to their own affairs.
To beings who had lived for centuries. One talented young Hero wasn’t particularly remarkable.
Thus Luke’s achievements became one of the hottest topics across the world.
Every kingdom discussed them. Merchants gossiped about them. Spies investigated them.
Demons quietly took notice. And countless young men became inexplicably jealous.
Fortunately Luke knew none of this.
Otherwise he would probably look at every one of them with complete confusion before asking,
"Did I run away with your wife? Then why the f**k all of you so jealous?"
Holy Light Church...
High above the clouds floated a colossal sacred island.
Its sheer size dwarfed many small continents, while hundreds of temples, cathedrals, and holy sanctuaries stood upon its surface.
Normally the Holy Light Church was a place of absolute tranquility.
The only sounds were hymns, prayers, and the ringing of holy bells.
Yet today a completely different atmosphere had formed.
Whispers spread throughout every corridor. Groups of clerics quietly exchanged glances.
Even the usually expressionless Holy Knights couldn’t hide their curiosity.
"Have you heard about the Hero?" One young cleric asked while carrying several ancient scriptures through a marble hallway.
His companion slowly nodded. "I have."
After this his face filled with disbelief and after making sure nobody was close enough to overhear them, he lowered his voice.
"...Did the Saintess truly make a mistake?"
The first cleric’s expression stiffened. When earliler he heard the rumor.
His immediate reaction had been denial. ’The Saintess...? Impossible.’
’She would never lie.’ Surely someone had fabricated the story.
However after verifying it through several official reports.
He discovered that Luke had indeed reached the Early Bronze Knight realm.
Not only that he had even slain a Mid-Golden Knight.
Everything was true. Which left him conflicted.
Should he rejoice? That the Hero chosen by the Goddess possessed extraordinary talent after all.
Or...
Should he mourn? Because the Saintess’s judgment appeared to have been wrong.
Unable to answer even himself. He merely shook his head.
On this the two clerics silently continued toward their destination.
Yet...
They were hardly the only ones. Throughout the Holy Light Church, Clerics. Holy Knights. Priests.
Even Bishops quietly discussed the matter.
No one could organize their thoughts. To every believer. The order of reverence had always been simple.
The Goddess.
The Saintess.
Then... The Hero.
Deep within the grand cathedral. A sacred silence remained.
Towering white pillars stretched toward an high ceiling.
Sunlight poured through huge stained-glass windows depicting the Goddess of Light.
At the center. The Saintess knelt before the divine statue.
Her white holy robes spread elegantly across the polished floor.
Her golden hair flowed gracefully behind her.
Her eyes remained peacefully closed.
She seemed completely detached from the world’s unrest.
Click.
A side door quietly opened. From which a female cleric entered before carefully approaching.
Without making unnecessary noise. She knelt beside the Saintess and whispered several words into her ear.
The Saintess’s eyes suddenly opened. For the first time in days. Genuine surprise appeared upon her beautiful face.
"Luke Voidheart..." and his name unconsciously escaped her lips.
Only fourteen days had passed since he had left.
Yet his entire life had seemingly changed.
"You’ve become strong..." She softly murmured. Which brings a faint smile on her lips.
Moments later that smile gradually faded.
And confusion replaced it.
’But... The Spirit Crystal wasn’t damaged.’
’So Luke should truly have been talentless.’
’Then... how?’
She replayed every detail of that day within her mind.
Every conversation, ritual and examination. Nothing seemed out of place.
No matter how much she thought. She found no answer.
The female cleric quietly observed the changing expressions upon the Saintess’s face.
She wisely remained silent.
Until The Saintess gently raised her eyes toward the enormous statue of the Goddess.
"It seems... this too was the Goddess’s will."
Her expression once again became filled with unwavering faith.
Perhaps The Goddess herself had secretly blessed Luke.
Perhaps this miracle had always been part of the divine plan.
Standing beside her the female cleric also bowed her head toward the goddess staute. "I believe so as well, My Lady."
If the System had been present, It would have exploded with outrage.
[This is fraud!]
[Why does my every contribution always go to some goddess.]
[First the Goddess of Luck, by Luke, and now even his talent goes to the goddess of light.]
The system would definitely argue with them for days.
Though if someone said this to him, "don’t worry about this."
"Maybe those goddesses will end up becoming his wives as well." then the system would gladly accept this.
Because of a hidden feature, which Luke didn’t know.
"My Lady." The female cleric finally spoke again.
"What should we do regarding the Hidden Hand?"
Upon this, the peaceful smile disappeared from the Saintess’s face. And a terrifying coldness silently emerged.
Only a handful of people within the Church had ever witnessed this expression.
Even the female cleric instinctively straightened her posture.
Then one word left the Saintess’s lips.
"Annihilation."
Her calm voice echoed throughout the cathedral.
The female cleric wasn’t surprised. As she had expected exactly this answer.
Attempting to assassinate the Hero personally chosen by the Goddess. Was no different from declaring war upon the Holy Light Church itself.
"Dispatch the Templar Knights." The Saintess slowly closed her eyes once more, after leaving those words.
And returned to prayer as though nothing had happened.
The female cleric respectfully bowed. "As you command."
After that she quietly left the cathedral.
The moment she stepped outside. She faced the waiting Holy Knights.
’It seems it’s time we show the world what happens if they touch their hero.’
Then her expression turned incomparably stern.
"Go."
"Erase the Hidden Hand from existence."
"Leave... not a single member alive."
The assembled Templar Knights struck their chests in salute.
"Yes!"
Brilliant holy auras erupted throughout the plaza.
Within moments the Church’s elite forces began mobilizing.
The Holy Light Church had officially entered the hunt.
Unfortunately Luke had no idea any of this was happening.
Otherwise he would probably be moved to tears.
"Finally someone actually stood up for me."
Of course his vampire wife had already done exactly that.
The only difference was. She preferred doing it from the shadows.

paragraphs: Inside the Hidden Hand Headquarters...
"Who accepted the Hero assassination request?" A deep, furious voice echoed throughout the dimly lit chamber.
The room fell deathly silent. While a long obsidian table stood at its center.
Twelve seats surrounded it. Upon each sat a figure cloaked in black robes, their faces hidden beneath deep hoods.
Every one of them radiated the overwhelming aura of a Diamond Knight.
Any one of these individuals alone possessed enough power to shake an entire kingdom.
At the head of the table...
A thirteenth chair stood slightly elevated above the others.
Upon it sat the organization’s leader. A Peak Diamond Knight.
Only a single step away from entering the realm of Kings.
A being capable of influencing the balance of entire kingdom.
Silence lingered for several seconds.
Finally one of the hooded figures slowly stood. His face had already turned deathly pale.
"It... was me." His voice carried obvious guilt.
He was the one who had approved the second assassination request against the Hero.
The moment those words left his mouth. Every gaze in the chamber slowly shifted toward him.
No one spoke, they merely stared at him. The looks in their eyes all conveyed the same message.
Idiot.
Not because he admitted his mistake.
But because he had actually accepted a contract targeting the Hero.
The leader’s eyes locked onto him.
For a brief moment it looked as though he might crush the man’s throat where he stood.
Fortunately he restrained himself.
"Shadow." His voice was frighteningly calm.
"Have you forgotten our motto?"
The atmosphere instantly became heavier. Because everyone remembered those words.
They had been engraved into the organization since the day it was founded.
"The Hand sees."
"The Hand knows."
"The Hand delivers."
Back then The Hidden Hand had been weak. Survival required caution.
So they gathered information first. Learned everything about the target.
Evaluated the risks. Only then did they decide whether to accept the mission.
Finally if the target was deemed acceptable. They delivered upon their promise.
That single motto had allowed the Hidden Hand to survive for centuries.
Unfortunately as the organization grew stronger. Many members gradually forgot its true meaning.
To them only the final part mattered.
"The Hand delivers." As long as enough money was offered.
They accepted any mission. Without considering the consequences.
Kings. Royal families. Ancient clans. Even organizations they should never provoke.
But money blinded them.
Shadow slowly lowered his head. Cold sweat trickled down his forehead.
"Leader..."
"Please forgive me this once."
"I swear I’ll never make the same mistake ne—"
"Next time?" The leader’s voice suddenly exploded.
His terrifying aura swept across the chamber.
Several Diamond Knights instinctively stiffened.
"You still think..."
"...there will be a next time?" His voice became even colder.
After a long silence. He slowly shook his head.
"We’re entering slumber." Upon this, the room instantly erupted.
"What?!"
"Leader!"
"You can’t be serious!"
Expressions changed one after another. Entering slumber meant suspending nearly every operation.
No assassinations, contracts and intelligence network.
Nothing for an entire century.
"But what about our overseas branches?" One hooded elder asked anxiously.
He had invested enormous resources into establishing one of those branches.
If it were abandoned his losses would be catastrophic.
The same concern appeared on several other faces.
The leader merely looked at them indifferently.
"As we speak, the lunatics from the Holy Light Church have likely already begun hunting us."
His cold gaze swept across everyone present.
"So Abandon every compromised branch."
The chamber fell silent once more. Everyone’s expressions became pale.
They all understood what that order truly meant.
Those abandoned branches. Were being sacrificed.
So before anyone could object with some nonsene. The leader stood.
His shadow gradually dissolved into darkness.
Just before completely disappearing. He spoke one final sentence.
"Shadow."
"You and your branch will serve as the bait."
"If you survive. I’ll allow you to return."
"If not, consider your debt repaid."
With this, his voice faded completely and the leader vanished.
Leaving behind a deathly silence.
Shadow remained frozen in place. His body trembled uncontrollably. One hand clutched his forehead.
While the other pulled tightly at his own hair.
Despair filled his eyes. He understood perfectly.
If he obeyed the order. The Church would undoubtedly kill him.
If he disobeyed. The Hidden Hand’s leader would personally hunt him down.
Either way...
Death awaited him.
The remaining members quietly watched his miserable state.
Yet not a single one mocked him. Nor did anyone offer sympathy.
Because...
Many of them had committed equally reckless acts in the past.
Accepting contracts against nobles. Royal families. and powerful organizations.
All for money.
Though this time Shadow had simply been the unlucky one.
One after another the hooded figures silently left the chamber.
Some immediately began preparing escape routes.
Others planned to disappear beneath new identities.
Within minutes the headquarters emptied.
Only Shadow remained.
Sitting alone in the darkness. Waiting for death to decide. Which side would reach him first.
VOLUME I END - A FAILED HERO.
Well... that was a hella journey;
As this is my first book. I don’t have many expectations for this.
But surprisingly, many new readers came and supported this work.
For that I AM TRULY VERY VERY GRATEFUL to all of you.
And special thanks to everyone who has supported this novel with GT, PS, Reviews and coins.
As all of you are life savers.
Ok... now, Volume II will start. So what’s to expect?
I will not spoil everything here, but a few things you can listen to.
The second volume will be focused on Kingdom building, territory expansion, so conflict will naturally follow.
One wife will also be going to meet Luke, so you are free to guess who she is. "◕‿◕"
New units, new artifacts, (Confirmed.)
New titans??? ( ̄_(ツ)_/ ̄)
And maybe, some harem members will also be spotted in the second volume.
Though no marriages for them.
That’s it, I guess.
And don’t worry, I am not taking a break, so the new volume will come as usual.
Also I don’t have any plans to drop this novel. So everyone can chill.
And if you leave a good review on the webnovel, it will also help this novel and me a lot.

chapters.title: Chapter 156: The Innocent Aurora | Why Doesn’t Master Love Me?
paragraphs: Aurora, who was peacefully eating breakfast alongside Vaelira, suddenly tilted her head.
"Huh?" She looked toward her master’s house in the distance.
"Why are those strange sounds coming from Master’s room again?"
Hearing her question, Vaelira paused midway through her breakfast.
The surrounding maids also looked at one another in confusion.
"What sounds?" Vaelira asked.
Aurora innocently blinked.
"The same sounds as yesterday night."
"Like this, Luke more~ Luke Faster, Luke cu-"
Before Aurora could continue...
Paf!
Vaelira hurriedly covered her mouth.
"Mmmph?" Aurora looked at her with completely innocent eyes, clearly wondering what she had done wrong.
Meanwhile...
The faces of every maid around the table instantly turned crimson.
Some lowered their heads. While others quietly focused on their breakfast.
’Lord seems quite energetic today.’
And the exact same thought appeared in several minds.
Vaelira’s own ears had already turned slightly red.
Looking at Aurora’s innocent expression, another thought surfaced.
’Is she truly this innocent?’
’Or is she doing this on purpose?’
After a moment, she slowly removed her hand.
Aurora immediately puffed her cheeks. "What did I do?"
Vaelira awkwardly coughed before trying to explain.
"Aurora, Master loves Aurielle very much, which is why, he is loving her in their room."
Aurora listened carefully.
Completely seriously.
A few seconds later, yearning appeared in her eyes.
"Then why doesn’t Master do that kind of love with me?"
Upon this the entire dining hall froze.
Even the servants carrying dishes nearby almost stumbled.
A silence so complete descended that one could hear the wind outside.
The maids faces became even redder. And several hurriedly looked away.
Vaelira herself became completely speechless. So before she could answer her question.
Aurora innocently continued. "Does Master not love me? Aren’t I Master’s creation?"
"Shouldn’t he love me too?"
Vaelira’s eyes widened.
Technically Aurora wasn’t wrong.
Luke certainly cared deeply for his summons.
The problem was the love Aurora was talking about.
The love between a husband and wife. Were completely different.
Unfortunately explaining that to Aurora was easier said than done.
After thinking for a while, Vaelira finally smiled.
"Master loves all of us."
"But the love he has for Lady Aurielle is different."
"It’s because she’s his wife and we’re like his family and companions."
Aurora blinked several times. She quietly thought about those words.
Finally she nodded. "I understand."
Then she immediately returned to her breakfast as though nothing had happened.
Seeing that the crisis had passed. Everyone secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
The atmosphere gradually returned to normal.
Although several maids still had noticeably red cheeks.
Even Vaelira absentmindedly touched her own face.
’...Would Master ever show us that kind of affection...?’ The unexpected thought appeared in her mind.
To which she immediately shook her head to drive it away. And no one noticed the brief flicker in her expression.
Fortunately...
Luke wasn’t there.
Otherwise, he would probably have shouted at the sky.
"System! What on earth have you been teaching my summons?!"
After all he had summoned them himself.
Yet he still had absolutely no idea where they originally came from.
Finally, Luke finished his long session of love with Aurielle, and after freshening up, both of them stepped outside.
"Hmph!" But Aurielle let out an embarrassed huff before walking toward the large garden they had built together, refusing to look back at him.
Seeing her reaction, Luke smiled sheepishly and scratched the back of his head.
A few moments later, he looked around and nodded in satisfaction.
From the very first day he obtained the Time Chamber.
He had wanted to turn it into their permanent home rather than just a place for training.
So, he had ordered every laborers present in the territory, to build an entire city inside it.
And finally after what amounted to a full year of time within the chamber.
It had been completed.
Luke turned around and looked at the simple two-story house standing peacefully amidst the greenery.
It was the home he shared with Aurielle.
Or at least...
It was where the two of them retreated whenever they wanted to do sex.
He shook his head, dismissing those thoughts, before looking around.
Everyone had already begun their daily routine.
Some were training. Some were cultivating.
While others were busy with construction or their assigned work.
Seeing the bustling city, Luke nodded in satisfaction before heading toward the Lord’s Office.
There was no doubt.
After conquering Windmarch Reach, the amount of work waiting for him had increased dramatically.
As he walked along the stone road, everyone he passed immediately stopped what they were doing.
"My Lord."
The knights saluted.
The maids bowed respectfully.
Even Osric and the other important officials greeted him with smile, before returning to their duties.
Luke acknowledged each of them with a slight nod as he continued forward.
A few moments later...
He arrived before a grand four-story building.
Click.
Pushing open the wooden doors, he stepped inside.
The spacious interior was elegantly decorated, with polished stone floors, sturdy wooden pillars, and neatly arranged furniture.
The building stretched nearly one hundred meters on each side.
Luke had intentionally ordered it to be built on such a large scale.
After all his territory would continue expanding in the future.
Naturally the number of officials would increase alongside it.
For now, however the building felt rather empty.
Only Luke occupied it.
Most administrative matters were currently handled by Osric together with the financial advisor, especially after Aurielle’s aunt had departed on a tour to neighboring territories.
Making his way to the second floor.
Luke settled into his chair before opening the large windows.
A cool breeze drifted inside, carrying the fresh scent of grass and flowers.
Only then did he pick up the stack of reports waiting on his desk.
The first report detailed the cleanup operation.
All the Body Temper spies and traitors had already been dealt with.
Depending on the severity of their crimes.
They had been sentenced to work in the Blackstone Mines.
Luke placed the report aside before thinking about those mines.
The Blackstone Mine produced a rare ore capable of forging weapons and armor suitable for Iron Knights.
Its value was enormous.
It was also one of the main reasons Baron Cedric and Viscount Aldric had always coveted the Blackstone Highlands.
The market for Iron Knight equipment was vast.
And Blackstone Territory possessed one of the richest deposits on the entire human continent.
In fact after personally estimating its reserves.
Even Luke had been stunned.
The total value of the ore buried beneath those mountains exceeded the two million gold coins currently stored in his treasury.
"So why hadn’t someone conquered this territory already?"
The answer was actually quite simple.

chapters.title: Chapter 157: The Corpse of a God
paragraphs: First.
Aurielle’s mother had become a noble after marrying the Human Emperor.
That status alone discouraged most nobles from openly attacking her territory.
The second reason. was the actual reason and was far more dangerous.
The Stormhowl Mountains.
The colossal mountain range separating the eastern territories from the Endless Forest.
A region rumored to shelter ancient Overlord Beasts.
Along with forgotten races that had once ruled Valtharion before retreating deep into the forest.
A large portion of the Blackstone Mine extended beyond those mountains.
During Aurielle’s mother’s reign.
The miners had gradually expanded deeper into the mountain.
Until..
They disturbed something that should not have been awakened.
An Evolved Beast.
A monster possessing the strength of a Golden Knight.
Its appearance nearly plunged the entire Blackstone Territory into disaster.
Fortunately Aurielle’s mother possessed a high-tier magic scroll.
Using it she managed to kill the beast.
However it had also been her greatest trump card.
Although the beast died, the territory also suffered devastating losses.
Thousands of soldiers perished. The mines were heavily damaged. And the treasury was nearly emptied.
To rebuild everything she had no choice but to borrow gold from Baron Cedric.
At an interest rate high enough to become a lifetime burden for her territory.
"...Poor woman." Luke quietly sighed.
Everything he knew about those events had come from Aurielle herself.
Naturally he had also asked where her mother was now.
The moment he asked Aurielle’s expression darkened.
Yet she chose not to answer.
Over time Luke had come to understand her better.
He could tell she wasn’t hiding the truth because she distrusted him.
She was trying to protect him. Though he still couldn’t understand why.
Perhaps...
Whatever secret surrounded her mother was something Aurielle believed he wasn’t ready to shoulder yet.
So Luke also didn’t press the matter.
’She’ll tell me when she’s ready’ With that quiet thought.
He leaned back in his chair, gazing silently at the ceiling.
That incident was precisely why mining operations had been halted for many years.
Only recently had Luke ordered them to resume.
At the same time, prisoners convicted of serious crimes were being sent there as laborers.
Murderers. Traitors. And those guilty of unforgivable crimes.
If they died while mining Luke wouldn’t lose any sleep over it.
Of course he didn’t send every criminal there.
Petty thieves and those who had committed minor offenses received lighter punishments.
After all he wasn’t short on money.
There was no need to squeeze every last coin from the mines at the cost of innocent lives.
Everything could proceed slowly.
Leaning forward once more, Luke picked up his quill and added another task to the list resting on his desk.
• Deal with the Stormhowl Mountains.
Sooner or later...
He intended to explore that place as well.
Beyond those mountains lay one of Valtharion’s greatest mysteries.
The Endless Forest.
A place said to contain treasures beyond imagination.
Yet not a single major power dared venture too deeply into it anymore.
Surprisingly The Endless Forest wasn’t what Luke had imagined.
Instead of stretching across the surface. It existed beneath the world.
An underground forest.
Its gigantic trees bore shimmering purple leaves, while their towering trunks disappeared into endless darkness.
No one had ever discovered where the forest truly ended. Or how deep it reached.
Countless expeditions had ventured inside. Almost all of them met the same fate.
Complete annihilation.
The terrifying Overlord Beasts lurking within rarely allowed anyone to return alive.
Yet even repeated failures failed to discourage the Human Emperor of that era.
Because of a single legend.
A legend claiming...
The Endless Forest concealed a path across the Endless Ocean.
The moment that rumor spread. The entire world descended into madness.
Since the Endless Forest existed beneath every continent.
Every race believed the hidden path might lie beneath their own lands.
For centuries exploration parties continuously entered the underground wilderness.
None succeeded.
Eventually most races abandoned the search.
Until one catastrophic decision changed history forever.
A group of Demi-Gods decided to explore the Endless Forest themselves.
The announcement alone shook the entire world.
Everyone believed if anyone could uncover its secrets.
It would be them.
And...
They did.
The Demi-Gods discovered the corpse of a god.
A true god.
At first the world celebrated. Until the next report arrived.
The corpse had awakened.
Within moments...
Every Demi-God who entered the forest was slaughtered.
Not one survived. But the nightmare didn’t end there.
The dead god emerged from the Endless Forest. And stepped onto the surface.
The result was exactly what anyone would expect.
An entire continent vanished.
Every kingdom. Every civilization. Every living creature.
Erased.
Even the mighty Overlord races. Whose armies had ruled Valtharion current Era.
Failed to survive more than a few seconds.
Terror spread throughout the world.
For the first time in countless generations. Every race truly feared extinction.
And so they prayed. Prayed desperately to their gods.
Finally the gods answered.
Not by descending personally. But by sending their Apostles.
One after another Divine Apostles arrived upon Valtharion.
The battle between them and the dead god lasted for months.
Its aftershocks devastated the entire world.
Tsunamis swallowed coastlines.
Earthquakes split continents apart.
Volcanoes erupted without warning.
Tornadoes consumed entire kingdoms.
Floods, Droughts.
Every natural disaster imaginable struck the world.
That war reminded every living being of one undeniable truth.
The gods were not myths. Nor were they beings mortals could ever hope to comprehend.
Eventually the Apostles prevailed. The battlefield itself shattered.
The continent where they fought broke apart into countless fragments.
Just when everyone believed the nightmare had finally ended.
The dead god’s body dissolved into a vast crimson miasma.
The crimson mist spread across the shattered land. Pulling every broken fragment back together.
Before the Apostles could stop it.
The corpse sacrificed itself. A gigantic crimson fissure tore open the heavens.
And from that crack...
Came the demons.
Luke had been stunned when Aurielle first told him this story.
Even now he still found it difficult to believe.
A search for treasure. Had ultimately unleashed the greatest catastrophe in Valtharion’s history.
"The Demon Continent..." Luke quietly murmured.
The continent where the dead god had emerged eventually became the homeland of the demons.
From that day onward. It was forever known by that name.
Scholars later proposed countless theories.
Perhaps a god—or even an Outer God—had died within Valtharion during the previous era.
But Gods were immortal.
Maybe its consciousness had perished. But its divine body had remained.
Perhaps...
Its final purpose had always been to summon the demons into this world.
Although no one knew the truth. That single incident revealed one thing.
Something unimaginably terrible had happened during the previous era.
Something significant enough to drive the gods away from Valtharion.
After that disaster. The great races officially abandoned all large-scale exploration of the Endless Forest.
Even today only treasure hunters and reckless adventurers dared enter its depths.
And nearly half of them. Never returned.
Luke shook his head, pushing those ancient stories out of his mind.
There would be plenty of time to uncover those mysteries in the future.
For now...
He picked up the next report. It detailed the recent war.

BLACKSTONE CASUALTY REPORT

| Golden Knights | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Silver Knights | 100 | 0 | 0 | 100 | 100 |
After seeing the report, his expression worsened. Because almost 80% of this occurred because of Golden knights.

Though, Luke didn’t know that his second wife, Selene, and the Saintess had already sent armies to erase them.
A few moments later he calmed down and noticed the numbers of Body Temper realm soldiers.
"Two thousand minus more, because all of them were traitors." He muttered with a thoughtful expression.
Even though the whole forces of the territory had reduced from 16 thousand to 8 thousand,
But currently he could defend only one territory with these numbers.
That’s why yesterday, he left all the forces stationed at Windmarch Reach, while returned back himself.
Because he had enough strength to defend the Blackstone Territory alone.
After that he checked the report of the Ashenford armies.
ASHENFORD ARMIES CASUALTY BREAKDOWN - 90% KILLED, 10% CAPTURED
| Category | Start | Killed (90%) | Captured (10%) |
| Golden Knights | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Silver Knights | 100 | 90 | 10 |
| Bronze Knights | 1,000 | 900 | 100 |
| Body Temper Soldiers | 50,000 | 45,000 | 5,000 |
"Hmm..." Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully. Because the number he was seeing was of the battlefield.
As some forces were still at Windmarch Reach, especially Body Temper realm, which was as high as 50,000 still left there.
"Fortunately, they didn’t resist hardly." Luke nodded, after remembering
that when they saw the Aether Devastation Beam Cannon, almost everyone’s morale instantly got destroyed.
While some Silver Knight elders retaliated, which resulted in a few getting killed and the remaining ones in jail.
Sadly, the report for loot or the gain had to be calculated, and it was gonna take some time.
"I hope their treasury has some good stuff." Luke smiled with expectation.
Then he brought the quill toward the paper and wrote more plans, which were needed for current territory development.
-Recruitment of new soldiers.
-Making a main road, connecting both territories, for easier transportation.
-Complete capture of surrounding towns, before other nobles could do that.
He only wrote these three with a serious face, because it was the priority.
As Luke just put the quill back-
DINGG!
The system notification sound immediately came.
How did he know that it was a system notification sound? Because the system had set it to annoy him.
So whenever he got rewards, this sound would follow suit.
But he didn’t yell or become angry at the system’s annoying sound, because who didn’t like money notifications.
[10,000x Return System Calculating Emotion of Previous Day.]
[Emotion Calculating...]
[Emotions: Love/Jealousy/Worried/Fear/Lust.]
"Heh??" Luke became annoyed, after seeing that Jealousy was still there.
"Why is she always remains jealous?" His face twitched, because he didn’t even go toward another woman, then from where was her jealousy coming?
[Kekeke. (¬‿¬)]
As he was in the middle of his thinking, the system’s weird laugh came, along with came the emoji.
"What?" He became baffled and asked him. On which he just continued the weird laugh.
So he ignored him and checked the other emotions.
"Worried and Fear." Reading this, he felt bad for Aurielle. Because he knew that when he said he would go and kill Aldaric by himself, she would have gotten so worried.
Still he shook his head and muttered. "For protecting you and our home, I did that."
"Lust."
With that he saw the last emotion and an image of Aurielle with her mouth full of his d**k came into his mind.
’So my Aurielle is the naughty type.’ A lewd smile appeared on his lips at this, while the system’s weird laugh continued.
[Kekekek. 🤭]
Fortunately, Aurielle was not here, as if she knew what Luke was thinking about her, then he would have to sleep outside for a month, alone.
After that he checked the system screen again.
[Reward Calculating...]
[1x Return triggered]
[Reward: E-Rank Aether Crystal Mine Blueprint]
[Base Quantity: 1]
[100x Base Return Activated]
[Reward Multiplied: 100 Aether Crystal Mine Blueprints]
[Rank: E-Rank (Bronze Knight Level)]
[Type: Enchanted Resource Production Blueprint]
[Production Capacity: 50 Perfect Aether Crystals per Month (Each Mine)]
[Quality: 100% Perfect Grade]
[Production Method: Automatically Absorbs Surrounding Aether → Crystal Formation]
"Finally!" Luke laughed excitedly, because his territory really lacked Aether crystals, which normally even a Baron’s territory had.
"Now I don’t have one, but freaking 100." His smile became wider and he also noticed the line.
"Perfect grade! Absurd!" Luke’s expression brightened upon seeing this and he thanked the system for its rewards, which always came top tier.
Because normally an Aether mine generated underground after a long duration, due to the concentration of Aether from the surroundings.
And each mine had to be excavated manually. Even then, the crystals contained impurities. Most were low-grade or standard-grade, only a handful reached high grade, and as for perfect-grade crystals.
Forget about it. Even after mining for days, finding a single Perfect Aether Crystal would be considered lucky.

"But mine produces them automatically and every single one is Perfect Grade." Luke laughed, imagining how wealthy he would soon become. Better yet, his troops would finally have a steady supply of Aether Crystals for cultivation.
And he remembered the chart, which he had seen during his earlier shopping.
AETHER CRYSTAL GRADES
| Grade | Quality | Market Price | Rarity |
| Low Grade | Impure, Small, Cloudy | 5-8 Gold | Common |
| Standard Grade | Average Purity | 10-15 Gold | Uncommon |
| High Grade | High Purity | 20-30 Gold | Rare |
| Perfect Grade | Flawless, Crystal Clear | 50-80 Gold | Very Rare |
Yes, a single Perfect Grade Aether Crystal could sell for up to 80 gold coins.
Which was simply incredible.
That meant one mine alone could generate around 4,000 gold coins every month.
And with a hundred mines. "Four hundred thousand gold coins every month!"
Luke’s eyes shone brightly as he calculated the figure.
While his laughter grew louder as thousands of possibilities flashed through his mind.
Then he suddenly paused.
"Wait a sec." He narrowed his eyes and his smile disappeared as he looked at the blueprint of the Aether Crystal Mine.
Because just now, he thought about the line. "It produces aether crystals by using surrounding Aether."
"I already have an aether-filled region." Luke muttered, because his time chamber was filled with a huge amount of Aether because of the Mana Well.
Even though the Mana Well produced the purest form of Aether, known as Mana, once it mixed with the surrounding air, it transformed into ordinary Aether.
Though, he didn’t pause for this. Instead he thought about the time chamber’s effect.
1:30 ratio.
This meant the production of his Aether Crystal Mines would far surpass those in the outside world, provided the Mana Well could supply enough Mana to sustain hundreds of them.
"I’m a genius." Luke shamelessly praised himself.
In response, the System displayed a speechless emoji on the screen.
Luke, however, completely ignored it.
Without wasting another moment, he left the building to find the perfect place to deploy all one hundred Aether Crystal Mines.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: The Jealous Wife’s Sigh
paragraphs: After stepping outside, Luke surveyed the surrounding area for a moment before his gaze settled on a vast open grassland.
It lay about a kilometer away from the main city.
A perfect location.
"Let’s do it, then." A smile of anticipation spread across his face, as he headed toward the open field.
Along the way.
Workers busy with construction, soldiers on patrol, and even knights in the middle of training noticed their lord’s unusually excited expression.
Curiosity immediately appeared on their faces.
"What is Lord planning now?"
After witnessing many miracles performed by Luke.
None of them doubted he was about to do something extraordinary again.
Since he hadn’t ordered anyone to follow or stay away. They simply watched from afar.
Then someone quietly muttered, "Maybe Lord is about to create another miracle."
The moment those words spread. Excitement swept through the crowd.
Without anyone giving an order. Those who could temporarily leave their work did exactly that.
One after another, they followed behind Luke with eager expressions.
As he walked, Luke naturally noticed the growing crowd behind him. He merely glanced back once.
Then smiled faintly. Since they wanted to watch. He saw no reason to stop them.
Aurielle was quietly enjoying the refreshing morning breeze, trying to clear her mind.
At first, she began thinking about how she should cope with the Luke increasing Lust..
Then—
’W-Why am I even thinking about that?!’
Her face instantly flushed crimson as she hurriedly shook her head, trying to drive those dirty thoughts away. but then...
From the corner of her eye, she noticed her perverted husband leading a large crowd of residents toward an open field.
"What’s he up to now?" Aurielle watched him thoughtfully.
Soon her mind connected his unusual behavior to her greatest rival.
’The Goddess of Luck?’ Her eyes narrowed dangerously.
But a moment later, her expression returned to normal.
"Sigh."
She still couldn’t understand it.
Why was the Goddess of Luck so interested in her husband?
Other than his excessive libido, caring personality, and overprotective nature...
She couldn’t think of anything that would attract a goddess’s attention.
"Perhaps she just wants to make the Goddess of Light jealous."
"Yet somehow, I’m the one, who becoming jealous." Another sigh escaped her lips.
Still she also began walking toward the same destination as Luke.
After all every gift from the Goddess of Luck had always been extraordinary.
Naturally, the others followed as well.
Aurora, Vaelira, Osric, Edmund. And many curious residents.
One after another, they headed toward the open field, eager to witness yet another miracle.
"This place." After arriving, Luke carefully surveyed the grassland once more before nodding in satisfaction.
Behind him rhe gathered crowd unconsciously held their breath.
Everyone waited expectantly for whatever miracle their lord was about to unveil.
Without any hesitation Luke reached into his System Inventory.
The next moment a blueprint appeared above his palm.
Although only a single blueprint floated there. A glowing ×100 hovered above it.
It represented one hundred Aether Crystal Mine Blueprints.
"Interesting..." Luke muttered while examining it closely.
The blueprint wasn’t shaped like an ordinary underground mine.
Instead it depicted a large cylindrical structure forged from dark stone.
Its specifications floated beside it.
Height: 5 meters.
Diameter: 3 meters.
And intricate azure runes covered its entire surface, pulsing rhythmically like a with the flow of Aether.
At its summit a slender Aether-collecting spire slowly rotated, continuously drawing Aether from the surrounding atmosphere.
Even in blueprint form. It was already absorbing ambient Aether.
While at the front, a single crystal panel glowed softly, waiting to be opened.
Luke smiled in satisfaction after seeing the blueprint’s simple design.
To everyone else, however it looked as though their lord was merely staring at his empty hand with a smile.
Aurielle watched him for a few moments before helplessly shaking her head.
So she lightly nudged his shoulder.
"Luke."
"Hurry up and show us what you’re planning this time."
Hearing her voice, Luke came back to his senses.
He smiled at her, then flicked his wrist.
The blueprint flew into the air.
The next moment, It split apart.
One...
Ten...
Fifty...
A hundred identical blueprints spread across the grassland before positioning themselves at perfectly equal distances.
The crowd stared in anticipation. A few seconds passed. Nothing happened.
The blueprints simply rested on the ground.
Confused, many people turned toward Luke, ready to ask what was happening.
Then—
RUMBLE!!!
A deafening tremor erupted across the Time Chamber.
The ground shook violently. Dust rose into the air.
Many spectators instinctively stumbled backward in fright.
Only Luke. Aurielle. Aurora. Vaelira. And Osric remained standing calmly where they were.
Soon before everyone’s eyes, large cylindrical structures slowly rose from beneath the earth.
One after another until all one hundred stood proudly across the field.
Each measured five meters in height and had a diameter of three meters.
Thousands of gasps echoed through the crowd. Even though they had expected another miracle from their lord.
But watching one hundred buildings emerge directly from the ground was beyond anything they had imagined.
Aurielle and the others also wore surprised expressions as they looked toward Luke. Silently waiting for an explanation.
On this Luke merely smiled. Instead of answering. He turned toward the gathered crowd.
"Everyone. Return to your duties."
Immediately disappointment spread across thousands of faces.
They desperately wanted to know what these mysterious structures were.
Still not a single person questioned their Lord’s order.
One by one they respectfully saluted before returning to their work.
Only Aurielle, Aurora, Vaelira, Osric, and Edmund remained. They understood Luke’s caution.
Although everyone inside the Time Chamber was bound by Aurora’s chains.
There were still methods capable of extracting memories. Mind-control. Soul-searching. Memory-reading.
If an enemy ever captured one of their people. Then Luke’s many secrets could be exposed. So the little they knew, that would be better.
That was why he intended to turn Blackstone Highlands into an impregnable fortress.
No outsider would enter without his permission. And no one would even come close to the Time Chamber.
As for the residents living here. Luke intended for them to remain inside permanently whenever possible.
"I just hope Aurora awakens an ability that can counter those techniques someday." Luke quietly muttered to himself.
A few moments later. Once everyone else had left. He finally explained the purpose of the structures.
"What the hell?!" But after hearing this, Edmund was the first to lose his composure.
Even Aurielle and Osric couldn’t hide their shock.
While Aurora had only one expression, ’My master is best.’ and Vaelira also smiled slightly toward Luke.
Feeling everyone’s stares. Luke coughed awkwardly.
"Each of these mines produces fifty Perfect Grade Aether Crystals every month."
"So from now on you can all cultivate without worrying about resources."
The moment those words sank in excitement appeared on each of their faces.
Only Edmund’s eyes shone for a completely different reason.
"My Lord, If we sell these crystals. We’ll earn an unimaginable amount of gold."
Luke smiled before shaking his head. "No. These crystals aren’t for sale."
"They’re resources for our own growth."
Hearing that Edmund’s shoulders immediately slumped. Although they had just conquered Windmarch Reach. And would soon receive a massive amount of wealth.
But he had also seen Luke’s long-term development plans.
Building roads. Expanding cities. Recruiting armies. Constructing fortresses.
Every single project required an enormous amount of gold.
So just as Edmund was about to persuade him once more.
Luke spoke again.
"Here is 1 million gold coins and some other things for the territory." Luke presented him with a spatial ring containing gold coins, agricultural seeds, ingots, tools, and weapons.
Which he had brought from the Count’s territory. But because of the earlier war, he hadn’t had the chance to give it to him.
"MY LORD... THIS!" Edmund’s expression became crazed, as though he had just witnessed something that could only exist in dreams.
’One million gold coins... and so many goods.’
Edmund felt he would be shocked to death by his lord one day.

For Osric, who earned only a few silver coins as salary, this sum was simply absurd.
As for Aurielle, she found it hard to believe that only a few days ago they had been a dirt-poor Baron territory.
Yet overnight, they had become wealthy enough to rival some lower-ranked Counts.
So with a slightly shaky voice, she asked,
"Luke..."
"Where did you get so much money?"
She asked out of pure curiosity, because the amount before her was simply unbelievable.
Hearing this, Osric and Edmund also raised their ears.
After all, they were Luke’s subjects, so they wouldn’t dare question their lord directly.
But Lady Aurielle. She was the boss of even Luke.
Unless, of course, he wanted to sleep outside for the night. Alone.
Luke’s mouth twitched after seeing Osric and Edmund’s shameless behavior.
He glanced toward Aurora and Vaelira, who were quietly looking at him...
Wait.
Not Aurora.
Her eyes were sparkling as though her master had suddenly become the richest person in the entire world.
’Aurora... don’t look at me with those eyes.’
So Luke hurriedly looked away before meeting Aurielle’s gaze.
On this She merely shook her head gently.
Perhaps she had only asked on impulse and didn’t actually wish to pry into his secrets.
Seeing that, a faint smile appeared on Luke’s face.
’This is also one of the reasons I love her.’
’Because she understands me.’
So Luke simply gave a vague answer. "I sold some of the things the Goddess of Luck rewarded me with."
Hearing this, Aurielle gave him a speechless look.
Meanwhile, Osric and Edmund exchanged puzzled glances.
’Our lord has connections with the Goddess of Luck as well?’
The next moment. Both of them slowly looked at each other.
Then identical sly smiles appeared on their faces.
’Our lord is playing with two goddesses... Hehe.’
Luke noticed those two sly smiles.
’What’s wrong with these two grown men?’
’Why are they smiling like gossiping aunties?’
But then he heard something which nearly freaked him out.
"Master is so Awesome!"
"That even the Goddess of Luck has fallen for you!" Aurora with an overjoyed expression said this.
Hearing this, Luke gave her an ugly look, ’Why Aurora...’
’Just why?’
And the next moment it happened, Luke felt the surrounding shadows become a little darker and even colder.
’Nah, it’s her gaze. That was colder.’
So with the expression of the world’s most innocent husband.
Luke slowly turned his head toward Aurielle.
She was smiling sweetly at him.
’Yeah...’
’Very sweetly.’
Luke also smiled back.
Though his smile looked more like someone standing before the execution platform.
Osric and Edmund also sensed the unusual atmosphere. So without exchanging a single word.
Both looked at one another. Then instantly ran for their lives.
’Traitors.’
Luke watched their disappearing backs from the corner of his eye before looking at Aurora, who still wore the same innocent expression, completely unaware of the disaster she had caused.
’Aurora...’
’No more chocolates for a month.’
After silently deciding her punishment, Luke immediately shouted,
"Honey! I suddenly remembered I have to meet the merchants!"
"Bye! Love you!"
The moment his words fell.
Valzerith Armor instantly enveloped his body.
FLASH!
Luke teleported one kilometer away.
"Phew..."
"I’m safe."
He wiped away nonexistent sweat before dismissing the armor.
Then...
"MASTER!!"
"SAVE ME FROM THIS CRAZY WOMAN!!"
Aurora’s miserable cry echoed across the entire city.
Luke immediately covered his face with one hand.
’Sorry, Aurora. I can’t save you this time.’
Silently he prayed for her.
Even though Aurora possessed the strength of a Golden Knight, she never resisted Aurielle during moments like these.
As a result Aurielle often dragged her to noble etiquette classes. Something Aurora hated more than training.
Luke shook his head helplessly.
But just then. He heard the distant roar of rushing water.
"Huh?"
’A waterfall?’
Confused, Luke frowned slightly. Only then did he realize. After teleporting away, he had been facing toward the city.
So He slowly turned around to see where the sound was coming from.
So Luke turned around and became shocked. ’Elena!’
Because there, Elena was bathing naked in the lake, as the waterfall from above dropped into the lake.
And she was looking at him shyly with a red face.
Upon this, Luke immediately covered his face and muttered. ’Why does this always happen to me!’
[Kekeke!]
Yeah, only the background music was left, which the system’s weird laugh completed.
"Master~" Then, Luke heard Elena’s little tipsy voice. ’huh? tipsy?’
So he removed his fingers slightly from his eyes and became shocked.
Because Elena had suddenly came in front of him and her big melons were bouncing back and forth, which he could see clearly. ’What the hell!’
But before he could process what was happening, Elena suddenly hugged him tightly with her naked body. "Master~"
Feeling her sudden touch on his chest and her tipsy voice, Luke froze in his place.
And even after a moment, when he felt she was not removing the hug, he immediately brought his shirt out of the spatial ring, before covering her naked body with it.
"Huuhh!" He released a safe breath, then noticed that Elena had slept in his arms.
What happened to her? "Elena." So he called out her softly, but she didn’t respond.
"She is hot." Not in that way, Because Luke felt her body temperature was rising fast and her whole body even became a little red from this.
"System, what’s happening to her?" Luke asked worriedly the system about her condition.
Because now, steam were also starting to release from her body, which freaked him out. ’Please nothing happen to her.’
[Hmm..., It seems like she is awakening her origin skill.] The system’s reply came, which baffled him.
"But why is her body becoming hot? Kai also awakened an origin skill and his body didn’t become hot."
Luke muttered, before picking Elena into a princess carry, while looking around where to bring her to rest.
[Luke, everyone shows different phenomena while awakening an Origin skill.] System added this, on which Luke paused and looked at Elena’s face, and she was repeating only one word.
"Master."
"Master."
"I am here Elena." So Luke said calmly to her, try to reassure her, but she seemed lost and couldn’t hear his words at all.
Seeing this, he became more worried and asked if there was anything he could do. "Tell me, how can I help her!"
His voice contained urgency, on which the System replied in a calm voice. [Just bring her back to the lake and be with her, until she awakens her Origin skill.]
Hearing this, his face became pale and he looked toward half-naked Elena, "If Aurielle saw me with Elena like that, then she would definitely make me castrate."
He muttered worriedly, but the system urged him to do it fast, or else her condition would deteriorate fast.
"Master, don’t leave me." Elena, in a sleep-like state, muttered this, while her face changed to fear. And she gripped Luke’s clothes tightly with her fingers.
Seeing this, he sighed and brought her back to the pool.
After submerging, he leaned her body toward him and hugged her.
Now they were sticking close together in a hugged pose, while Luke caressed her hair slowly to calm her down.
"I am here, Elena." He also muttered this gently, on which Elena’s grip on his clothes lessened, but her hug became tighter.
’I hope Aurielle will not see this.’ Luke hoped these, but rather than Aurielle, someone else was seeing everything.
The person who likes to note her master’s successful womanizer list, Vaelira.
’Elena also fell in love with master.’ She added her name to the list as well, while keep looking at Luke.
If Luke was here, then he would definitely flick at her forehead and shouted. "What’s wrong with my summons!"
But he should be glad that Vaelira was here, not Aurora, or else she would have said, "I also want to bathe with Master."

chapters.title: Chapter 161: The Distance Between Them
paragraphs: Previous Day...
Elena watched worriedly as her master fought the Mid-Golden Knight alone.
Yet she could do nothing.
’Why am I so weak?’
Her golden eyes became moist as the same thought surfaced once again.
Because after the day her master had summoned her. He had only relied on her once.
After that, he never came to ask for her help again.
That fact always left a strange emptiness inside her heart.
So she devoted herself to helping the people of the territory instead.
Healing every wounded knight and injured soldier to the best of her ability.
But when she heard that Master was about to leave for the Count’s territory.
She suddenly felt alone.
Alone, despite being surrounded by her nine mage friends and the maids.
Unlike Aurora, she never openly asked to stay beside her master.
But deep inside she always wanted to spend more time with him.
She always wanted to remain by his side.
So whenever she saw Lady Aurielle, Master’s wife, clinging to him and rarely leaving his side.
A faint jealousy would unknowingly rise inside her heart.
Lady Aurielle could stay beside Master whenever she wished. While she was always left behind.
Elena didn’t know whether she alone felt this way.
But no matter how hard she tried. She simply couldn’t stop those emotions.
"Master!" Her face turned pale after seeing him groan in pain as he returned to his human form from his Titan transformation.
The sight made her heart ache. So without hesitation.
She poured every last drop of mana from her body into healing him.
’Please...’
’Never do something like this again, Master!’ She cried those words inside her heart.
Yet she couldn’t bring herself to say them aloud. Even she coudn’t understand why.
After being healed. Master didn’t return to rest.
Instead he immediately headed back toward the battlefield.
To rescue everyone still fighting there.
Even though she knew Master was right. And she also felt heartbroken seeing so many people dying on the battlefield, especially Master’s own subjects.
But a selfish part of her still wished. That Master had chosen himself. That he had stayed safe.
But she also knew. That was impossible.
Because Master had to go. As he was the strongest person in the territory.
Stronger than anyone else.
’Why am I so weak?’
Once again, the same question echoed inside her heart.
Her friends had noticed her expression earlier and even asked if something was wrong.
But she couldn’t say anything. Not a single word.
After arriving at the battlefield, the scene before her made her breathing stop.
Bodies covered the ground. Many soldiers had already lost their lives.
Others lay crying, screaming, or groaning in unbearable pain.
Seeing that her heart ached once more.
Even though her body hadn’t properly recovered after exhausting all of her mana healing Luke.
Elena pushed herself to her limit again. Because she wanted to save everyone.
She didn’t want a single person to die.
"Save me!"
"Please... save me!"
"I can’t hold on!"
"I... I’m dying..."
One desperate cry after another reached her ears.
The moment she landed on the battlefield, she rushed toward those in the most critical condition.
Healing. Running.
Healing again.
Again.
And again.
She managed to save many lives.
But...
Many more slipped away before her eyes. Some whose bodies had been crippled cried in despair.
Others whose organs had been pierced or shattered slowly died while enduring unimaginable pain.
She watched every one of them. Yet she could do nothing.
"WE WON!!" Suddenly, cheers erupted across the battlefield.
Elena instinctively turned toward the center.
There her Master stood surrounded by everyone.
He had defeated the enemy Golden Knights. Victory belonged to Blackstone.
Seeing him safe, a faint smile finally appeared on her exhausted face.
But when she turned back. The soldier she had been treating...
Had died, with his eyes wide opened.
Seeing this, something inside Elena. Quietly broke.
The brilliance in her golden eyes dimmed slightly as she lowered her gaze.
Her hands were covered in blood.
After several long moments. She slowly looked toward her master once again.
Then...
A terrible thought entered her mind.
’What if one day, I couldn’t even heal master?’ Her breathing became unsteady.
’Will Master... die as well?’ With every passing thought. The light inside her eyes grew dimmer.
Beside her, the doctors of Blackstone Territory kept calling her name.
But Elena couldn’t hear them anymore. Her entire world had become silent.
And only one thought remained.
’Will Master really... die?’
Slowly she turned toward the doctor calling her.
The moment he saw her eyes. He instinctively stepped backward in fear.
Her pale golden eyes had almost completely lost their warmth.
Yet Elena paid no attention to his reaction.
Instead she quietly looked toward Luke.
He was smiling while talking with Lady Aurielle.
"Why am I so weak, Master?"
She whispered beneath her breath, hoping to get an answer.
But that whisper Luke could never hear. Because he was nearly one kilometer away.
After watching him for several more seconds. without getting any answer.
She slowly stood up. With vacant eyes. And turned around before silently walked back toward the territory.
Back to the Time Chamber.
Back to the quiet lake beside the mages residences.
While Luke remained busy conquering Windmarch Reach.
Upon returning home. The other mages immediately noticed something was wrong with Elena.
Luna, Mira, Tara, and the others hurried over with worried expressions, asking what had happened.
But Elena simply shook her head. Without saying a single word.
She dragged her exhausted body into her house. Then quietly lay down on her bed.
That entire night. She couldn’t sleep peacefully.
Every time she closed her eyes. The same nightmare returned.
Master was covered in blood.
Calling her name.
Reaching out toward her.
Yet. No matter how desperately she healed him...
Her magic accomplished nothing. His wounds wouldn’t close. And his heartbeat slowly faded.
Until he died before her eyes.
"NO!"
Elena suddenly sat upright with a terrified scream.
Her breathing was ragged as cold sweat soaked her clothes.
She hurriedly looked around. The room was silent.
"It... was only a dream..."
Just as she tried calming herself. A sharp itching sensation spread across her upper back.
"Ugh..." She winced in pain. And trying reach her hand behind herself and felt two swollen bumps beneath her skin.
As though something was trying to emerge from inside her body.
"Elena!" The door suddenly burst open.
Luna, the Nature Mage.
Mira, the Water Mage.
Tara, the Earth Mage.
Along with the remaining six mages, rushed inside with worried expressions.
"What happened, Elena?"
"Are you alright?"
Their voices were filled with concern.
Then each of them noticed her eyes.
The warm golden radiance they were familiar with. Had become noticeably dimmer.
But Elena didn’t seem to notice their worried expressions.
Instead, she simply forced a weak smile and gently shook her head.
"I’m fine..."
"It was just a bad dream."
Even as she said those words. Her dull golden eyes betrayed her.
They had lost much of their former brilliance, as though the light within them was slowly fading.
The nine mages exchanged worried glances.
None of them believed her.
But seeing the exhausted smile she was forcing onto her face, none of them had the heart to press her any further.
Although they didn’t believe her words, they respected her wishes.
Each of them reminded her to take care of herself and told her not to hesitate if she needed anything, before leaving her room.
Still Mira chose to remain behind.
Even though Elena insisted she was fine, Mira still stayed beside her.
