paragraphs: The next morning...
When Elena slowly opened her eyes, she found Mira sleeping peacefully beside her.
A gentle smile appeared on her pale face.
Not wanting to wake her friend, Elena quietly climbed out of bed and headed toward the lake for a bath.
As she walked outside, weakness spread through her entire body.
Her skin also felt much hotter than usual.
Even so, she ignored the discomfort and continued walking toward the lake.
After confirming that no one else was there.
She quietly removed her all clothes and stepped into the clear water.
"Cold." A relieved sigh escaped her lips.
The cool water soothed the burning heat inside her body, making her feel slightly better.
However the itching around her upper back only became stronger.
"W-What’s happening to me?" She muttered weakly as her vision gradually blurred.
The entire world seemed to sway before her eyes.
Then she noticed someone standing in the distance.
"Master~" She called out to Luke.
Her voice sounded strangely soft and slightly intoxicated.
Yet she didn’t notice the difference herself.
With unsteady steps, she slowly walked toward him.
’Huh?’
’Why is Master covering his eyes?’
’Does master not want to see my face anymore??’ thinking this, she felt afraid.
Afraid that master had found she was useless and didn’t want to see her face again.
’No!’ So she increased her strength in her legs, and just as she reached near Luke, she hugged him tightly, or atleast tried, but could only increase her grip on his clothes.
Though, just as she did this, her vision spun and she became unconscious.
Present Time...
While hugging Elena’s body, he felt some swelling on her upper back.
"What’s this?" he touched the part and became confused, because it seemed something was trying to come out.
Then it happened. Without any warning, two angel wings suddenly came out from her upper back and it was still containing some blood, likely when they came out.
Luke got startled from this and tried to back away, then remembered that Elena was still unconscious, and saw her dropping into the water, so he hurriedly reached out and held her waist tightly.
As he sighed in relief after catching her.
Elena’s eyes suddenly snapped open. They had turned completely golden, devoid of any pupils, as two pillars of radiant light shot from her eyes straight toward the heavens.
While Luke was getting shocked from the phenomenon, inside him, the three titans were sleeping.
But suddenly two snapped open their eyes, Nyx and Caelith, then with narrowed eyes, they looked toward the sky.
Likely trying to see something between Elena and the heavens themselves.
The system, who was watching the whole phenomenon from the start, became surprised after seeing both titans reaction.
And thought, ’A real titan is something.’ Even though they had lost their original power, they were still able to see the divinity in the sky, which was really something.
Because perceiving divinity normally requires one to be at the Demi-god realm or above, or possess a special ability, such as an Origin Skill related to it.
Then the system also looked upward, likely toward the heavens themselves. ’Seems like she was watching Luke all this time.’
At this, an amused smile appeared on the system’s face. Then he looked toward Elena, muttered thoughtfully.
’Hmm... Valtharion is allowing them to make some changes to an Origin Skill.’
[Interesting.] the System remarked, causing Luke to frown in confusion.

"What’s interesting?" But the system didn’t reply, at which he shook his head, because he had come to understand already that his system was something different, not like the slave systems he had read about in novels or comics.
[Hey! Who are you calling a slave! (╯°□°)╯( ┻━┻] The system’s angry words came out, but this time Luke ignored this.
Fortunately, the light emitting from Elena’s eyes had stopped and her breathing was also returned back to normal.
At this, he sighed in relief and smiled at her. But then his eyebrow twitched.
Because due to her angel-like feathers, which suddenly came out from her upper back, the clothes he had put on her were shredded and dropped into the water.
So Elena was again fully naked.
But this time, he noticed something different. "She has become more beautiful."
Luke really felt her face had a different glow, like a heavenly aura, which mortals couldn’t touch, and even her body was glowing with a golden glow.
[So Luke you are noticing her beauty now. I already told you before, that you should have made these mage’s already fall in love with you. 😒]
As he was commenting on her beauty, the system’s voice came, along with an annoyed emoji.
"I never said they are not beautiful. Especially for Elena." Luke gave him a speechless look and brought another of his clothes to cover her body fully.
Because maybe someone close to this location would come here after noticing that golden light.
So he didn’t want the pervert label on him.
Fortunately, the wings she had summoned had returned to her upper back and only a small swelling could be seen again, but no wounds.
"Master." The thing he was worried most happened.
Luke froze while dressing Elena, and with a robot-like body, he turned toward the sound.
There Mira, the water mage, was standing with her hand on her mouth, while a deep red blush could be seen on her cheeks, as she looked at him and the half-naked Elena.
"Mira." Luke softly called out her name, on which she nodded with a smiling face. But her gaze still didn’t move from the hand which was holding Elena.
’What is she thinking?’ Luke became confused, while Mira was shouting excitedly inside.
’Elena already won master’s heart!’
’Yeah! I have to tell the others as well!’
If Luke really found out her thoughts, then he would had given her a speechless look, while saying.
’Girl, I don’t want people to find anything about this situation and you are thinking about spreading this?’
’Don’t you want your master to live anymore?’
’Because if my wife finds out about this, then think just a little bit how your poor master will survive.’
Sadly Luke didn’t know this and could only hope that this talk wouldn’t reach Aurielle’s ears.
Fortunately, Vaelira who saw everything from a distance, would keep quiet about everything.

"Ahh, Master. Elena seems ill, that’s why she was resting earlier. But I didn’t know when she came out by herself." Elena, when she came out of her fantasy thoughts, muttered in panic, while giving a sorry pleading look to Luke.
Though at this Luke just sighed and carried Elena out in a princess carry out of the lake, before giving her to Mira and said.
"Just be careful next time." And turned to leave, but-
He stopped as Elena was holding his clothes with a tight grip, and her face had again become like she was in some kind of nightmare.
Seeing this, both Luke and Mira paused. And Mira said worriedly, "Master, Elena is like this from yesterday."
Hearing this, Luke also become worried, so he caressed her forehead gently, while saying, "I am still here, Elena, don’t worry."
After saying this, he saw Elena’s face expression relaxed a lot, like hearing his voice had an effect.
Then he removed her hands gently, before deciding to follow them as well.
In case something like this happened again, so he could take care.
After a few moments later, they reached Elena’s house, while Luke chose to stay outside. At this Mira said how could that be, but Luke just said.
"First take care of Elena." And pointed toward her dress, which was still not fully covered and her private parts could clearly be seen.
Seeing this, Mira became embarrassed and hurriedly shut the door in Luke’s face.
’Yeah, my summons are weird.’ With that Luke sat down beneath one tree and checked Elena’s profile.
"Let’s see what Origin skill she had awakened." Luke said with expectation, because the earlier phenomenon suggested it should be a higher rating.

chapters.title: Chapter 163: The Goddess’s Secret Intervention
paragraphs: [Status/Summoned/Mage.]
[Elena Whitemore]
[OVERVIEW]
Attribute: Details
Full Name: Elena Whitmore
Title: Light Mage / Healer
Realm: Early Circle Mage (Early Bronze Knight Equivalent)
Origin Skill: Heaven’s Embrace (S-Rank)
Status: Alive
Affiliation: Blackstone Highlands
Role: Primary Healer / Support Mage

Luke’s gaze lingered on the newly unlocked system feature, which brings a hint of curiosity across his face. It seemed the system had granted this function as well, the moment he advanced to the Bronze Knight realm.
"Hmm... now checking the data of summons can be done much more easily." A faint smile appeared on Luke’s lips as he gave an approving nod.
Without wasting another moment, he checked Elena’s status. His eyes immediately landed on her realm.
Early Circled Mage.
A trace of surprise flashed through his blue eyes before he nodded in understanding.
Like the Knight cultivation path, the mage’s first two realms also followed a simple nine-stage progression.
The Mana Awakening Realm. Then the Apprentice Mage Realm.
However, everything changed after that. The Circled Mage Realm no longer had nine stages.
Instead, it was divided into only four ranks—
Early. Mid. Late. Peak.
To step into the Early stage, a mage first had to condense an Arcane Mana Circle around their heart.
That process alone demanded incredible precision.
Even the slightest instability could cause the circle to collapse.
Only after the Arcane Mana Circle became completely stable and perfectly formed, would the breakthrough truly succeed.
At that exact moment, the mage would officially enter the Early Circled Mage Realm.
And that was the realm Elena had successfully reached.
For this, every mage followed a different path.
Some relied on relentless daily training. While few consumed precious potions.
Others devoted themselves to learning higher-tier spells.
And many sharpened their abilities through repeated battles, polishing their magic with every life-and-death encounter.
As for Elena, she had reached this stage through nothing more than daily meditation.
Luke couldn’t help but feel impressed.
’Amazing!’ And a faint smile formed on his lips.
That alone was enough to prove just how extraordinary her talent truly was.
To advance further into the Mid-Circled Mage stage, a mage had to continuously strengthen and refine the Arcane Mana Circle surrounding their heart.
The methods remained the same—
Training. Potions. Advanced spells. And hundreds of battles.
Recalling everything he had learned during his visit to the Mage Tower, Luke gave a small nod before shifting his attention to Elena’s Origin Skill.
But the very next second, his eyes widened slightly.
"...S-rank?" A flicker of astonishment surfaced across his face.
"Elena is certainly lucky to awaken an Origin Skill of this rank." saying this, bring a smile escaped his lips as he opened its description, completely unaware of the truth.
Originally, Elena’s Origin Skill had only been A-rank.
However...
The Goddess of Light herself had personally intervened, using a fragment of her divine power to elevate it to S-rank.
And Luke, knew nothing about it.
The true reason remained known to only the Goddess of Light.
[Origin Skill - Heaven’s Embrace (S-Rank)]
Description: *The Light That Would Not Fade.*
"There are moments in every soul’s life when the darkness grows so deep that even the light within begins to flicker.
Elena Whitmore had such a moment. She had given everything—her mana, her body, her very will—and still, people died before her eyes. Still, her master bled. Still, she was not enough.
In that silence, in that despair, a wish was born. Not a prayer. Not a plea. Just a single, desperate thought that refused to die: ’I will not let him fall.’ And something answered.
Something ancient. Something that had no name and no origin. It reached through the cracks of reality and touched her soul, planting a seed that grew into wings.
Heaven’s Embrace is not a gift. It is the answer to a cry that was never spoken aloud."
Luke’s expression gradually darkened as he finished reading the description.
And a trace of sadness appeared in his blue eyes.
He had never realized that Elena had been carrying so much pressure on her shoulders all this time.
"...Poor girl." This brings a guilty smile appeared on his lips before quickly fading away.
Afterward his gaze slowly dropped to his own hand.
He had promised himself that he would become a better husband.
Yet somewhere along the way, he had forgotten that he was also a lord.
And more importantly, the master of every summon who had entrusted their lives to him.
"I never even tried to understand them." Murmuring softly, Luke leaned against the tree before lifting his eyes toward the sky above.
Silence followed.
Then, one after another images surfaced in his mind.
Aurora. Vaelira. Kai. Elena. His other mages. His soldiers.
Every summon who had crossed paths with him.
Each face appeared before his eyes, only to be replaced by another.
The more he thought about it. The heavier his heart became.
If Elena had been hiding so much pain behind her gentle smile.
Then-
’What about the others...?’ That single thought weighed on his chest like a stone.
His shoulders slumped as a weary sigh escaped his lips.
"I have to start paying more attention to them as well." His eyes softened with newfound resolve.
Then, taking a slow breath, Luke lowered his gaze and began reading the description once more.
However the instant his eyes reached the final line—
His mouth twitched.
"Heh... since when did you become a poet?" Luke let out a dry chuckle as he mocked the system.
The very next second—
A translucent screen popped up before him.
[(¬_¬") What?] Along with came the system’s irritated voice, which echoed in his mind.
It had spent considerable effort crafting those masterpiece descriptions.
Yet instead of appreciating them, Luke was making fun of its creativity.
Luke glanced at the floating emoji before raising an eyebrow.
"Since when did you start writing riddles in your descriptions?"
Without waiting for an answer, he continued.
"And what’s this ’something ancient, which has no name’?" His expression gradually turned serious.

chapters.title: Chapter 164: Your Elena~? | The Caught Husband
paragraphs: "Are you telling me? that something interfered with Elena’s awakening?"
Every question he asked had come from details he had noticed while reading the system’s description.
For a brief moment. Silence lingered.
Then the screen flickered once.
[I already gave you a hint. I’m not telling you anything more. ( ;)]
The system replied in a slightly annoyed voice.
And the next instant. The screen vanished.
"Huh..." Luke blinked.
"After becoming poetic, you’ve changed." He muttered under his breath, sounding genuinely surprised.
Still he didn’t dwell any further on the mysterious ancient existence.
Not yet.
If the system had considered it a genuine threat, it would have warned him directly.
At least, that was what Luke believed.
Because his previous conversations with the system had taught him one thing—
Whenever real danger was involved, the system never remained silent.
With that thought, he let the matter rest and shifted his attention to Elena’s abilities.
[PASSIVE ABILITY: Divine Warmth]
{Even passive abilities require the user to activate their Origin Skill, which continuously consumes Aether or Mana. Otherwise, a passive ability would remain active indefinitely.}
Details: Elena’s presence radiates a gentle, comforting light that passively soothes and heals nearby allies.
Effect: Allies within a 100-meter radius (the range increases with the user’s realm) gradually recover from minor wounds and fatigue over time.
"Her Origin Skill is good." Luke nodded with satisfaction after reading the description.
After all, not every Origin Skill possessed a passive ability.
Take Rowan, for example.
His Earth Giant Origin Skill granted him different Origin abilities, yet it didn’t provide a single passive effect.
Aurielle, however, was different.
Her passive ability naturally enhanced her control over shadows, allowing her to wield them with greater precision and ease.
Seeing these examples, Luke couldn’t help but form a theory.
It seemed that the higher the rank of an Origin Skill, the greater the chance it had of possessing a passive ability.
Though, it wasn’t an absolute rule.
[ABILITY 1: Holy Sanctuary]
Type: Active / Area Buff
Description: Elena creates a small sacred zone where allies are continuously healed and protected from negative effects.
Range: 15-meter radius
Effects:
• Continuous Healing: Allies inside the sanctuary recover health slowly over time.
• Debuff Purification: Minor curses, poisons, and negative status effects are gradually removed.
• Damage Reduction: Allies take slightly less damage while inside the sanctuary.
"She seems to have inherited the Light element’s traits almost perfectly." Luke muttered thoughtfully as he finished reading the description.
After all...

Among all the known forces, only the priests and holy knights of the Holy Light Church—the very church whose Goddess had summoned him—were renowned for resisting curses and purifying darkness, poison, and other malevolent effects.
And now he had someone capable of doing the same. thinking this, a satisfied smile slowly spread across his face.
"Looks like I have one on my side as well." With that thought, Luke’s curiosity grew.
So without another pause, he shifted his gaze to Elena’s next ability.
[ABILITY 2: Guardian Light]
Type: Active / Shield & Heal
Description: Elena wraps a single ally in a protective cocoon of holy light, healing their wounds and shielding them from harm.
Effects:
• Heal: Restores moderate health to the target.
• Shield: Creates a barrier that absorbs incoming damage.
• Resistance: Grants temporary resistance against curses and darkness.
"A single-target ability, nice." Luke nodded with a satisfied smile.
There was hardly any need to comment further.
After all, everyone knew the value of a protective shield in battle.
But this one went a step further. It didn’t just protect the target—
It healed them as well.
That combination alone made the ability exceptionally valuable.
"Finally!" Luke’s eyes lit up with anticipation.
"Her ultimate." And a hint of excitement surfaced on his face as he looked at the final ability.
After all...
Regardless of an Origin Skill’s rank—
Its Ultimate Ability was always awesome and crazy.
[ULTIMATE ABILITY: Wings of Salvation ⭐]
Type: Ultimate / Area Healing & Buff

Description: Elena’s angelic wings unfurl from her back, As they spread open, a brilliant golden radiance erupts outward, bathing the battlefield in holy light. Throughout the duration, the wings continuously release waves of holy energy that heal, protect, and bless every ally within range.
Range: 500-meter radius
Effects:
• Full Heal: Completely restores the health of all allies within the area.
• Cleanse: Removes all curses, poisons, debuffs, and other negative status effects.
• Divine Shield: Grants every ally a holy barrier that absorbs incoming damage for a short duration.
• Holy Blessing: Increases resistance against darkness, corruption, and other evil energies.
• Stamina Restoration: Completely removes fatigue and restores physical and mental stamina.
"Okay..."
"...That’s crazy." His eyes widened in genuine shock.
Even though his own Titan abilities were ridiculously overpowered. Elena’s Ultimate was no less astonishing.
His gaze remained fixed on the description. The first thing that caught his attention was the range.
"A 500-meter radius; at the Circled Mage Realm?!"
He couldn’t help but exclaim. That alone was absurd.
Within such an enormous area, every ally could be covered by the spell. It was simply broken.
Then his eyes swept across the effects once more.
Complete healing.
Removal of every negative status effect.
A divine shield.
A holy blessing.
Stamina restoration.
One after another...
Each effect was powerful enough to be considered an ultimate ability on its own.
If an ordinary healer possessed even one of these effects. Then yhey would be treasured by an entire kingdom.
"But my Elena has all of them." Luke slowly shook his head. "That’s insane."
"Your Elena~?"
But then a sweet, teasing voice suddenly drifted into his ears from behind.
Luke froze. His body stiffened almost instantly.
A dangerous premonition crept into his heart.
’...I know that voice.’
’The same voice, which he shut yersterday night with his mighty d**k.’
’But now it’s here again.’
In an instant, every bit of Luke’s earlier excitement vanished.
While a nervous smile crept onto his face as he slowly turned around.
’There she was.’ Standing behind him was a breathtaking black-haired beauty.
Her mesmerizing purple eyes were locked onto him. While a sweet smile rested on her crimson lips.

For a brief moment.
Silence lingered.
Then the screen flickered once.
[I already gave you a hint.
I’m not telling you anything more. ( ;)]
The system replied in a slightly annoyed voice.
And the next instant.
The screen vanished.
"Huh..." Luke blinked.
"After becoming poetic, you’ve changed." He muttered under his breath, sounding genuinely surprised.
Still he didn’t dwell any further on the mysterious ancient existence.
Not yet.
If the system had considered it a genuine threat, it would have warned him directly.
At least, that was what Luke believed.
Because his previous conversations with the system had taught him one thing—
Whenever real danger was involved, the system never remained silent.
With that thought, he let the matter rest and shifted his attention to Elena’s abilities.

{Even passive abilities require the user to activate their Origin Skill, which continuously consumes Aether or Mana.

Effect: Allies within a 100-meter radius (the range increases with the user’s realm) gradually recover from minor wounds and fatigue over time.

After all, not every Origin Skill possessed a passive ability.
Take Rowan, for example.
His Earth Giant Origin Skill granted him different Origin abilities, yet it didn’t provide a single passive effect.
Aurielle, however, was different.
Her passive ability naturally enhanced her control over shadows, allowing her to wield them with greater precision and ease.

It seemed that the higher the rank of an Origin Skill, the greater the chance it had of possessing a passive ability.
Though, it wasn’t an absolute rule.

Type: Active / Area Buff
Description: Elena creates a small sacred zone where allies are continuously healed and protected from negative effects.
Range: 15-meter radius

• Damage Reduction: Allies take slightly less damage while inside the sanctuary.

Regardless of an Origin Skill’s rank—
Its Ultimate Ability was always awesome and crazy.

chapters.title: Chapter 165: The Honeytrap Along With An Seductive Offer
paragraphs: A smile so gentle...
...that it felt more terrifying than an army of monsters.
In her hand, she held the imaginery purple sword, which she raised slowly-
One clearly aimed at castrating something.
’Huh...? Castrate?’
But before he could process the thought—
[Luke! that’s a freaking real sword! RUN!]
The system’s panicked shout exploded inside his mind.
Luke’s eyes widened to their limits.
Without a moment’s hesitation, he threw himself backward.
CRACK!!
And the next moment a crack sound echoed through the Mage’s Residence Area.
Aurielle’s sword flashed like a streak of violet light, slicing cleanly through the massive tree beside him as though it were made of paper.
For a split second, the tree remained standing.
Then—
BAAAAM!!
It crashed onto the ground with a loud roar, sending dust and leaves flying in every direction.
Luke stared blankly at the fallen tree. While a cold bead of sweat slowly trickled down his temple.
Then another.
He silently wiped his forehead, forcing a stiff smile.
’...That was way too close.’
"My Elena~?" Luke heard Aurielle’s sweet voice once again.
This time, however, her gaze slowly drifted downward. Toward his soaked clothes.
’huh? Why the heck are my clothes still wet?’ Luke’s heart skipped a beat. And a wave of panic washed over him.
’Don’t tell me! she saw Elena and me at the lake?’
Maintaining a rather stiff smile, he forced himself to speak. "H-Honey. weren’t you with Aurora?"
The moment those words left his mouth. Aurielle’s smile disappeared. It was replaced by a slight frown.
’Seems like Aurora ran away again.’ Luke sighed inwardly, though his eyes never left Aurielle’s face.
"Darling~" Her gentle voice rang out once more.
"Would you mind explaining~ why you’re in the Mage Bath Area~"
She paused. "...with your clothes completely wet~?"
As the last word left her lips. She took a slow step toward him.
Instinctively—
Luke took one step back.
Seeing that, Aurielle’s lips twitched ever so slightly.
Without saying another word, she took another step forward.
And Luke also took another step back.
The distance between them remained exactly the same.
For a brief moment...
Silence filled the forest. Only the sound of rustling leaves echoed between the two. and the system speechless emoji. [0-0]
"Darling~" Aurielle tilted her head slightly.
"Why are you backing away?" She said, with a gentle smile on her lips.
"Why don’t you come over here and give me a hug~?"
’Aurielle! At least look at my face before saying something like that!’
Luke roared inwardly.
Because, her beautiful purple eyes weren’t looking at his face.
They were fixed at his little brother.
Then his eyes slowly shifted toward the gleaming purple sword in her hand. Which seems to had blood on its edge.
’Hell no!’ So without the slightest hesitation, he shook his head so vigorously it was almost a blur.
There was absolutely no way he was getting any closer.
Watching his reaction, Aurielle’s smile stiffened.
A faint vein pulsed on her forehead as irritation quietly surfaced in her eyes.
She knew perfectly well that Luke could escape whenever he wanted.
If he truly decided to run. She wouldn’t be able to stop him.
That was precisely why she had tried a gentler approach. using honeytrap.
Lure him close. Wrap him in her sweet words.
Then...
Interrogate him lovingly- ’Cough!’.
Question him lovingly.
Unfortunately, her husband had chosen survival over romance.
If Luke could have heard her inner thoughts. He would have screamed without hesitation.
’Are you out of your mind?! Who tries to "Question lovingly" while holding a freaking! bloodstained sword?! And where did that blood even come from?!’
Which innocent soul had already, sacrificed by her hand.
Seeing honeytrap was not working. She thought about something different and a few moments later.
Aurielle’s eyes suddenly lit up, as though a brilliant idea had crossed her mind.
Which brings a sly, enchanting smile curved her lips.
"Darling~" Her sweet, seductive voice flowed into Luke’s ears like honey.
"How about tonight... we try those positions from your world."
She deliberately paused before adding with a teasing smile,
"...the ones you’ve always wanted to try~?
The moment those words reached him. Luke felt the fear in his heart lessen.
Instead several of those "special" positions from his previous world involuntarily surfaced in his mind.
One after another.
He licked his lips, thinking those.
So before he could even realized. He had become completely lost in his imagination, where he was riding Aurielle.
[Luke! Wake up! Just look at her hand!]
Suddenly system’s urgent shout exploded inside his mind.
[Do you seriously think, that your little brother will survive long enough to try any of those positions?]
"Huh?!" Luke instantly snapped back to reality. Because system word hold truth and wiped away his lar, which was dropping to the ground.
But next moment, his eyes widened. Only then did he realize.
Without him noticing in the slightest. Aurielle had already shortened the distance between them by several steps.
’Honey trap!’ Luke inwardly cursed the tactic.
The terrifying part was...
It had actually worked on him.
Taking a slow breath, he forced a gentle smile onto his face and spoke in the most loving tone he could manage.
"Honey."
"Why don’t you put that sword back into your Spatial Ring first?"
He chuckled awkwardly. "Then we can sit down and talk nicely."
"You know... like we always do."
Hearing those words, Aurielle came to an abrupt stop.
"...Tch." She clicked her tongue in annoyance.
She genuinely hadn’t expected her usually horny husband to escape her little honey trap so quickly.
"Fine." Letting out a reluctant sigh, she dismissed the purple sword into her Spatial Ring.
After all, if she kept holding it, Luke would probably flee the moment she took another step.
However—
The instant the sword disappeared...
Whoosh!
Luke suddenly appeared right in front of her.
"Wha—!"
Aurielle’s beautiful purple eyes widened in surprise.
But before she could even react.
Luke gently clasped both of her hands within his own. His grip wasn’t forceful. It was warm and reassuring.
’Now I’m safe.’ Luke silently sighed in relief.

chapters.title: Chapter 166: The Shameless Husband
paragraphs: As long as both of her hands were occupied. She couldn’t suddenly pull out another sword.
With that comforting thought, he leaned forward, intending to steal a quick kiss.
Yet...
Aurielle simply turned her face to the side. His lips missed their target.
Keeping her gaze averted, she asked in a calm, suspicious voice,
"Why did you say? ’My Elena’?" The teasing smile from earlier had completely vanished.
Hearing her suspicious voice, Luke mouth twitched at his wife always suspicious behaviour.
Though, earlier in the lake something did happened. But that was not his fault at all.
So he explained everything to Aurielle, from the start of Elena Awakening to the finding her Origin skill, And how happy he had been after seeing her incredible abilities.
Naturally, He left out one tiny detail. Very tiny, that its mentioning would not had any effect at all.
The fact that Elena had been completely naked.
Instead, Luke described the scene in the most innocent way possible.
According to his narration. Elena had been dressed in thick, modest robes.
From head To toe.
Not a single inch of skin had supposedly been visible.
Luke even emphasized it several times, nodding earnestly as if trying to convince both Aurielle...
...and himself.
Aurielle listened quietly from beginning to end.
She didn’t interrupt even once.
However, the more Luke talked about Elena’s clothes. The more suspicious Aurielle’s expression became.
Her beautiful purple eyes narrowed ever so slightly.
’Why is he talking so much about her clothes?’ And question mark practically appeared above her head.
Meanwhile.
The system watched the entire performance from the sidelines.
It let out a long, exhausted sigh.
’He really should’ve brought Margaret into his harem.’
’At least she could’ve kept Aurielle under control.’
A floating emoji appeared before Luke.
Even the system looked utterly speechless.
Luke blinked at the emoji.
He had absolutely no idea, what the system was trying to tell him.
Fortunately, Luke realized he was overacting and decided to stop digging himself into a deeper hole.
Afterward, without another word, he stepped closer and swiftly captured Aurielle’s lips.
"Mmph..."
Caught off guard, Aurielle’s eyes widened for a brief moment.
Then, her tense shoulders gradually relaxed. The suspicion in her eyes also softened, if only a little.
After sharing a long, lingering kiss, Luke slowly pulled away, resting his forehead against hers.
"So..." He smiled gently. "What brought you here?"
Aurielle took a small breath, to remove the blush from her cheeks, before answering.
"Osric has been looking for you."
Her expression returned to normal as she continued.
"Almost every merchant passing through the Blackstone Highlands has gathered outside."
"And many new merchant caravans have arrived as well."
"They all wish to meet you, to discuss the toll fees."
Luke blinked.
"Oh..." Only then did he remember why he had left in the first place.
As soon as Aurielle finished speaking. She shot him an irritated glare.
After all, not long ago, he had confidently declared that he was going to meet the merchants.
Yet somehow, he had ended up in the Mage Residence instead.
"Sorry, Honey." Luke laughed awkwardly before apologizing.
To make up for it. He quickly stole another couple of kisses from her lips.
"Mmph..."
Aurielle helplessly shook her head.
There was simply no winning against her shameless husband.
Letting out a quiet sigh, she intertwined her fingers with his.
The two of them turned around, preparing to leave together.
But just then—
"Master!"
A panicked voice suddenly echoed from inside the house.
"Elena’s condition doesn’t seem right!" Mira’s anxious cry instantly erased the lighthearted atmosphere.
Luke and Aurielle’s expressions changed at the same time.
Without another word. Both of them rushed toward the house.
Without slowing down, they pushed the door open and stepped inside.
The scene before them made both of them freeze.
Elena was lying on the bed. Her entire body trembling uncontrollably.
She repeatedly shook her head from side to side, as though desperately trying to escape from an invisible nightmare.
Tiny beads of sweat covered her forehead.
Her clothes were completely drenched. Even the bedsheet beneath her had become soaked.
"Elena..." Luke called her name softly, his voice filled with concern.
He carefully walked toward her. And Aurielle silently followed at his side.
"Master." The instant Elena heard Luke’s voice.
Her tightly shut eyes suddenly snapped open. And her pupils had already returned to their familiar golden color.
The moment she saw him. A faint light flickered within them.
They were glistening with tears.
It seemed, she had been crying even in her sleep.
Without thinking, Elena hurriedly tried to get out of bed.
However, her trembling body refused to cooperate.
She nearly collapsed the moment her feet touched the floor.
Fortunately, Luke had already reached her.
He quickly caught her before she could fall, gently supporting her shaking body with both of his arms.
"Master." Elena called out to him once again. Her trembling voice was barely above a whisper.
Luke gently nodded, his expression softening.
"It’s alright."
"Calm down."
However, tt was as though Elena couldn’t hear him.
She desperately clutched onto his clothes with both hands.
"Master..."
"P-Please don’t throw me away."
Her voice cracked.
"I-I won’t become useless..."
"I’ll work harder..."
"I’ll become stronger..."
"Please..."
"...don’t abandon me."
One sentence after another poured out of her trembling lips.
Words she had buried deep within her heart.
Words she had never found the courage to say.
Until today.
The nightmare had shattered the walls she had built around those fears.
It had forced every suppressed emotion to the surface.
She was terrified.
Terrified that one day...
Her master might truly cast her aside.
Unable to hold herself together any longer. Elena completely broke down.
Tears streamed endlessly from her golden eyes as heart-wrenching sobs echoed throughout the room.
The entire house fell silent.
No one spoke. No one interrupted.
They could only watch as the girl who had always smiled quietly.
Finally let out all the pain she had been carrying alone.

Without thinking, Elena hurriedly tried to get out of bed.
However, her trembling body refused to cooperate.
She nearly collapsed the moment her feet touched the floor.
Fortunately, Luke had already reached her.
He quickly caught her before she could fall, gently supporting her shaking body with both of his arms.
"Master." Elena called out to him once again.
Her trembling voice was barely above a whisper.
Luke gently nodded, his expression softening.
"It’s alright."
"Calm down."
However, tt was as though Elena couldn’t hear him.
She desperately clutched onto his clothes with both hands.
"Master..."
"P-Please don’t throw me away."
Her voice cracked.
"I-I won’t become useless..."
"I’ll work harder..."
"I’ll become stronger..."
"Please..."
"...don’t abandon me."
One sentence after another poured out of her trembling lips.
Words she had buried deep within her heart.
Words she had never found the courage to say.
Until today.
The nightmare had shattered the walls she had built around those fears.
It had forced every suppressed emotion to the surface.
She was terrified.
Terrified that one day...
Her master might truly cast her aside.
Unable to hold herself together any longer.
Elena completely broke down.
Tears streamed endlessly from her golden eyes as heart-wrenching sobs echoed throughout the room.
The entire house fell silent.
No one spoke.
No one interrupted.
They could only watch as the girl who had always smiled quietly.
Finally let out all the pain she had been carrying alone.

chapters.title: Chapter 167: The Teasing Wife
paragraphs: Seeing Elena break down like that. Both Mira and Aurielle felt their hearts ache. Sadness filled their faces.
The nightmare hadn’t merely frightened Elena. It had completely shattered her emotional defenses.
"I’m not throwing you away." Luke’s gentle voice reached her ears.
Carefully, he raised his hand and slowly wiped away the tears streaming down her cheeks.
At his touch, Elena slowly lifted her head.
Her tear-filled golden eyes met Luke’s calm blue ones.
With a trembling sob, she asked,
"R-Really...?"
Luke answered with nothing more than a warm smile.
Then he nodded.
"Of course." He softly brushed a loose strand of hair behind her ear before saying,
"Why would I throw away my best healer?"
Those simple words carried far more warmth than any grand promise.
Elena’s sobs gradually began to subside.
Seeing that, both Aurielle and Mira exchanged relieved smiles from the side.
Luke continued, his voice gentle yet firm.
"And even if one day, you decide that you want to leave me."
He smiled faintly.
"I still won’t let you go."
"Do you understand?"
Hearing her master reassuring voice. And looking into the warmth reflected in his smiling eyes.
Elena slowly wiped away the fresh tears gathering at the corners of her eyes.
A small, fragile smile finally bloomed on her face.
"...Mm." She nodded gently.
Then, Elena quietly leaned forward and wrapped her arms tightly around him.
"I’m sorry, Master..."
Her muffled voice came from against Luke’s chest.
"For causing so much trouble."
Hearing those words, Luke simply smiled. He gently stroked her soft hair.
"It’s alright."
"You don’t have to apologize."
However, No reply came.
Luke blinked. Curious, he leaned back slightly to look at her face.
Only then did he realize. Elena had already fallen asleep once again.
A helpless smile appeared on his lips. "You really exhausted yourself."
Carefully, making sure not to wake her, Luke lifted her slightly before gently laying her back onto the bed.
He pulled the blanket over her and tucked it around her shoulders.
Then he turned toward Mira.
"Mira."
"Take good care of her."
"And if anything unusual happens inform me immediately."
His voice became noticeably more serious.
As he spoke, he handed Mira the Whispering Tide Conch for instant communication.
Mira accepted it with both hands before nodding firmly.
"Yes, Master." A gentle smile appeared on her face as she sat beside Elena’s bed, quietly watching over her sleeping friend.
Luke gave one last glance toward Elena. Seeing her peaceful expression at last...
He also silently let out a breath of relief.
"Let’s go." With those words.
Luke and Aurielle quietly left the room, gently closing the door behind them so Elena’s sleep wouldn’t be disturbed.
"Fufu~" The moment they stepped out of the house, Aurielle’s teasing laughter reached Luke’s ears.
"I never knew, that my husband was so good at calming women down."
Luke chuckled before puffing out his chest proudly.
"Heh."
"Honey, you have no idea just how talented your husband really is."
A smug grin spread across his face.
Seeing his shameless expression. Aurielle simply rolled her beautiful purple eyes.
"Talented."
She let out a small snort.
"only in bed."
Luke’s smile instantly froze. The corner of his mouth twitched.
Just as he was about to fire back with a witty retort—
Aurielle spoke again before he even had the chance.
"I have some work to take care of."
She casually waved her hand.
"You can deal with those merchants by yourself."
With that, she turned around and gracefully walked toward the city, her long black hair swaying gently behind her.
Luke watched her retreating figure before smiling helplessly.
"Alright." He gave a small nod toward her back.
Then he turned in the opposite direction. Without lingering any longer.
He headed toward the exit of the Time Chamber.
It was finally time to meet the waiting merchants.
2nd day of flora month, same year.
When Luke stepped out of the Time Chamber. It was still morning.
Warm rays of sunlight poured through the long hallway windows, painting golden streaks across the polished stone floor.
The mansion had already come to life. Servants hurried from one room to another. While knights stood proudly at their posts.
The atmosphere was peaceful.
"Greetings, My Lord!"
The guards immediately straightened their backs and saluted as Luke passed by.
Luke acknowledged them with a small nod. "Mm."
Without slowing his pace, he continued toward the grand reception hall.
By now almost every merchant passing through the Blackstone Highlands had gathered there.
Even many unfamiliar merchant groups had arrived, eager to discuss future trade.
As Luke walked through the corridor...
His footsteps suddenly slowed. "Hm?"
Standing motionless beside a decorative suit of knight armor, was a figure wrapped entirely in bandages.
From head to toe. Not even a strand of hair was visible.
The person stood so still that they looked more like an statue than a living human.
Luke blinked.
’Since when did we have a mummy inside the mansion?’ Curiosity immediately surfaced in his eyes.
Unable to resist. He quietly changed direction and walked toward the mysterious figure.
One step. Two steps. Three.
Soon, he was standing only a few feet away.
Luke leaned forward slightly, narrowing his eyes.
’The bandages look surprisingly real.’
He slowly circled around the figure, observing it from different angles. ’Should I. touch it.?’
Just as that dangerous thought crossed his mind—
"My Lord."
The mummy suddenly spoke.
"W-What the hell?!" Luke jumped backward in pure reflex.
His eyes widened. His heart nearly leaped out of his chest.
He instinctively put several steps between himself and the "mummy," staring at it as if it had just come back from the dead.
For a few awkward seconds. Silence filled the hallway.
Then Luke slowly calmed his breathing.
He looked at the bandaged figure once more. And a strange expression appeared on his face.
’Fantasy mummies can actually talk?’
Before Luke could continue wondering. The "mummy" spoke again.
"My Lord." A brief pause followed.
"It’s me. The Osric." The voice sounded unusually weak. Muffled.

chapters.title: Chapter 168: The Holder Of Many Titles, Luke
paragraphs: As though its owner had been beaten so thoroughly that even speaking had become a challenge.
"Osric?" Luke blinked several times. His eyes slowly widened in disbelief.
"What happened to you?!" His voice carried genuine concern.
"Who in the world was cruel enough to do this to you?" For a brief moment. Luke truly pitied him.
Osric, however, merely gave him a long. Completely speechless stare.
"My Lord." He sighed weakly.
"I ended up bearing someone else’s wrath."
"Because a certain someone never showed up to meet the merchants."
Luke’s smile immediately stiffened.
Osric continued in a lifeless tone.
"So."
"I went to look for that certain person."
"...Then I happened to run into Lady Aurielle."
He slowly raised one heavily bandaged hand. Pointing at himself. "And this happened."
After saying that. He lowered his head in grievance.
His entire posture screamed ’I was an innocent victim.’
Silence.
Luke silently looked at Osric.
Then a certain image flashed through his mind.
The purple sword. And the faint bloodstain along its edge.
’No wonder Aurielle’s sword had blood on it.’ A cold shiver ran down his spine. Goosebumps instantly covered his arms.
He looked at Osric again. From head to toe.
Wrapped in bandages. Barely recognizable.
His expression gradually filled with sympathy.
’Poor Osric.’ Then another thought suddenly crossed Luke’s mind.
’Wait...’
’If Aurielle had found me first instead of Osric.’
He unconsciously swallowed. His hand instinctively moved to protect his lower body.
A chill ran straight down his back.
’I would’ve lost far more than a little blood.’
Looking at Osric now. Luke couldn’t help but feel relieved.
At least someone else had become the sacrifice this time.
Then Luke couldn’t help but think to himself.
’It’s your karma, buddy.’
’You ran away earlier and now you’re just harvesting the fruits of your own actions.’
Naturally, he wisely kept those thoughts to himself.
The poor man had already suffered enough. There was no need to pour salt into his wounds.
With that.
Luke and the heavily bandaged Osric continued toward the gathering hall.
Their footsteps echoed softly through the mansion’s long corridors.
A few moments later.
The two arrived before an enormous hall.
It had originally been built to host large banquets and noble celebrations.
However since the rapid development of the Blackstone Highlands.
It had gradually become the territory’s official meeting hall, where important guests and large gatherings were received.
Even before reaching the entrance. Luke could already hear hundreds of voices coming from inside.
Merchants discussing. People laughing. Several conversations overlapping with one another. The constant chatter blended into a lively hum.
Luke raised an eyebrow. ’Just how many people are in there?’
Even he was surprised by the sheer amount of noise.
Taking a steady breath. He stepped forward.
The guards stationed beside the huge wooden doors immediately straightened.
"Greetings, My Lord!"
However.
Their eyes instinctively drifted toward the "mummy" standing beside Luke.
Both guards exchanged puzzled glances. One of them almost failed to suppress his curiosity.
’When did a mummy join Lord Luke’s entourage.?’
Fortunately.
Years of discipline stopped him from asking such a suicidal question.
Without another word, both guards respectfully pushed open the huge wooden doors.
Creeeak.
The heavy doors slowly swung inward.
The old hinges produced a long, deep creaking sound that echoed throughout the vast hall.
Almost instantly. The bustling conversations came to an abrupt halt.
One after another, the voices disappeared.
Within only a few heartbeats. The lively hall fell into complete silence.
So quiet that even a pin dropping could probably be heard.
Every head turned toward the entrance.
Young and old. Men and women.
Seasoned merchants and newly arrived traders alike.
Hundreds of curious eyes simultaneously settled on the doorway.
Because almost every merchant who had entered the Blackstone Highlands was already gathered inside.
So naturally, the same thought appeared in everyone’s mind.
’Who could possibly be arriving now?’ Their curiosity only grew stronger.
However, when they finally saw the person entering through the doorway. They were all stunned.
A figure wrapped entirely in bandages appeared. From head to toe.
For a brief moment. Everyone instinctively stared at the "mummy."
Questions immediately surfaced in their minds.
’Who is that?’
’Is he injured?
’Or is he some mysterious powerhouse?’
But those thoughts lasted only a moment.
Soon their gazes naturally shifted away from the bandaged figure.
Toward the young man walking calmly at the front. The true reason they had all gathered here.
Baron Luke.
The Hero Luke.
The so-called Talentless Hero.
The husband of five princesses.
The lord of the Blackstone Highlands.
The owner of many titles.
Each merchant knew him by a different title.
Yet...
None of them were certain whether the title "Talentless Hero" still suited him anymore.
After all.
His rise to the Early Bronze Knight Realm without relying on any publicly known precious resources had completely overturned that old rumor.
If someone like that was truly talentless. Then what were ordinary people supposed to call themselves?
Still. Among all the stories surrounding Luke.
There was one fact that every merchant believed without the slightest doubt.
His combat power rivaled a Mid-Golden Knight. That single thought lingered in everyone’s mind.
It was precisely because of that terrifying strength. that they had more willingly chosen to travel through the Blackstone Highlands.
Previously, anyone wishing to reach the Ashveil Trade Route had only two choices.
The first. Pass through Blackstone.
The second. Take the old mountain route.
A path filled with steep cliffs, dense forests, magical beasts, roaming bandits, and countless hidden dangers.
A single mistake there. Could easily cost someone their life.
Compared to risking everything on that perilous journey.
They also had to deal with bandit forces. Not ordinary bandits. But groups secretly backed by powerful nobles.
Those criminals frequently set up illegal checkpoints, demanding "protection fees" from passing caravans.
More often than not. The merchants had no choice but to pay.
Otherwise, they risked losing both their cargo and their lives.
As a result, their transportation costs increased significantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 169: The Smug Smile
paragraphs: But now...
Everything would be changed.
’We can receive the backing of a Mid-Golden Knight.’ That single thought filled the minds of nearly every merchant present.
In truth.
When Viscount Aldaric wanted to occupied the Blackstone Highlands, many merchants hadn’t opposed it.
Some had even welcomed it. The reason was simple. He was a Mid-Golden Knight.
With someone of that strength overseeing the territory, almost no bandit force dared to approach the Blackstone Highlands.
That alone had greatly reduced their losses while making the trade route much safer.
Now...
Baron Luke—the husband of the territory’s original past owner—was rumored to possess the very same level of combat power.
Naturally they hoped to build the same relationship with him.
After all they had already been using the Blackstone Highlands as one of their regular trade routes for quite some time.
If they maintained a good relationship with Baron Luke.
Perhaps...
He would even show them a little leniency when it came to the toll fees.
At least that was the hope each merchant secretly carried.
Thinking of this. Many of the merchants quietly exchanged glances.
Some smiled politely. Others remained expressionless.
A few, however openly looked at one another with hostile eyes.
Because every merchant gathered here understood one thing.
The people standing beside them. Were also their competitors.
And none of them wanted to see their rivals secure better terms before they did.
That was precisely why many of them had brought expensive gifts. The presents had been neatly arranged in one corner of the hall.
Each gift bore the sender’s name.
Beside them, a young maid diligently recorded every merchant’s name onto a parchment, ensuring no contribution would be overlooked.
Luke swept his gaze across the mountain of gifts before a faint smile appeared on his lips.
"Thank you all for waiting." His calm voice echoed throughout the spacious hall as he stepped inside.
Behind him the heavily bandaged Osric quietly followed, looking every bit like a walking mummy.
Their attention quickly returned to Luke.
The very next second. Every merchant respectfully bowed.
"Greetings, Baron Luke!!!" Their loud voices echoed across the hall.
Warm smiles decorated every face. Some even lowered their heads a little further than necessary.
Deep inside many silently thanked their lucky stars.
Fortunately they had never openly mocked Baron Luke in the past.
Even those who had once looked down on him had only done so behind closed doors.
Never in front of him.
Otherwise they would have been standing here today with nothing but regret.
Seeing the scene before him a faintly smug smile slowly spread across Luke’s face.
He couldn’t help but recall the past. When he had first arrived in the Blackstone Highlands.
He had wandered through the territory several times.
Back then many of these very same merchants had crossed paths with him.
Yet not a single one had greeted him.
Some hadn’t even bothered to acknowledge his presence.
To them he had merely been the talentless hero. An insignificant baron living in a remote territory.
But now...
Luke slowly swept his gaze across the hall.
One familiar face after another entered his sight. He recognized quite a few of them.
The irony wasn’t lost on him. The same people who had once ignored him. Were now standing respectfully before him.
Smiling. Greeting him with enthusiasm. Treating him as someone worthy of their utmost respect.
’Heh... hypocrites.’ Luke shook his head inwardly.
Still he didn’t let those thoughts show on his face.
Maintaining a calm expression, he walked toward the elevated platform at the end of the hall.
Several broad marble steps led to a single seat reserved exclusively for the lord of the Blackstone Highlands.
His seat.
Step. Step. Step.
The sound of his footsteps echoed throughout the silent hall.
Reaching the top, Luke calmly turned around before taking his seat.
His gaze swept across the gathering below.
"You may all sit." His voice wasn’t loud.
Yet it carried enough authority for everyone to hear clearly.
"Thank you, Sir Luke."
One after another, the merchants bowed before taking their seats on the rows of chairs arranged neatly beneath the platform.
The previously tense atmosphere eased slightly.
Meanwhile...
Osric quietly walked toward the corner where the gifts had been placed.
Ignoring the curious looks directed at his bandaged appearance, he simply stood there with his hands behind his back.
Luke rested one arm on the throne’s armrest before slowly examining every face in the hall.
His eyes calmly moved from one merchant to another.
Experienced traders. Young successors. Representatives of merchant guilds. Not a single expression escaped his notice.
Then.
His gaze paused for a brief moment.
Sophia.
A faint smile appeared on Luke’s face. He gave her a small nod.
Sophia politely returned the gesture with a graceful smile before quietly lowering her head again.
Only then did Luke shift his attention back to the crowd.
"So..." He folded his hands together.
"For what reason has everyone gathered here today?" His calm question echoed across the hall.
The merchants collectively twitched.
’Sly bastard.’ Several of them cursed inwardly.
’As if he doesn’t already know why we’re here.’ Everyone understood perfectly well.
Luke was intentionally making them speak first.
That way whoever opened the negotiations would lose the initiative.
It was a classic bargaining tactic. And they had all fallen into it.
For a few moments...
Silence lingered throughout the hall.
The merchants exchanged subtle glances, silently urging one another to take the first step.
Finally one middle-aged merchant slowly rose from his chair.
As soon as the merchant stood up. Every gaze in the hall shifted toward him.
Luke’s blue eyes also settled on the man.
Despite becoming the center of attention. The merchant remained completely composed.
Not even the slightest hint of nervousness appeared on his face.
He was an elderly man in his fifties. His neatly combed white hair gave him a dignified appearance.
Several expensive rings adorned his fingers, each embedded with a different gemstone.
His luxurious robes were woven from high-quality fabric, while every accessory he wore silently proclaimed one thing—
Wealth.

sentences.text: But now...
Everything would be changed.
’We can receive the backing of a Mid-Golden Knight.’ That single thought filled the minds of nearly every merchant present.
In truth.
When Viscount Aldaric wanted to occupied the Blackstone Highlands, many merchants hadn’t opposed it.
Some had even welcomed it.
The reason was simple.
He was a Mid-Golden Knight.
With someone of that strength overseeing the territory, almost no bandit force dared to approach the Blackstone Highlands.
That alone had greatly reduced their losses while making the trade route much safer.
Now...
Baron Luke—the husband of the territory’s original past owner—was rumored to possess the very same level of combat power.
Naturally they hoped to build the same relationship with him.
After all they had already been using the Blackstone Highlands as one of their regular trade routes for quite some time.
If they maintained a good relationship with Baron Luke.
Perhaps...
He would even show them a little leniency when it came to the toll fees.
At least that was the hope each merchant secretly carried.
Thinking of this.
Many of the merchants quietly exchanged glances.
Some smiled politely.
Others remained expressionless.
A few, however openly looked at one another with hostile eyes.
Because every merchant gathered here understood one thing.
The people standing beside them.
Were also their competitors.
And none of them wanted to see their rivals secure better terms before they did.
That was precisely why many of them had brought expensive gifts.
The presents had been neatly arranged in one corner of the hall.
Each gift bore the sender’s name.
Beside them, a young maid diligently recorded every merchant’s name onto a parchment, ensuring no contribution would be overlooked.
Luke swept his gaze across the mountain of gifts before a faint smile appeared on his lips.
"Thank you all for waiting." His calm voice echoed throughout the spacious hall as he stepped inside.
Behind him the heavily bandaged Osric quietly followed, looking every bit like a walking mummy.
Their attention quickly returned to Luke.
The very next second.
Every merchant respectfully bowed.
"Greetings, Baron Luke!!!" Their loud voices echoed across the hall.
Warm smiles decorated every face.
Some even lowered their heads a little further than necessary.
Deep inside many silently thanked their lucky stars.
Fortunately they had never openly mocked Baron Luke in the past.
Even those who had once looked down on him had only done so behind closed doors.
Never in front of him.
Otherwise they would have been standing here today with nothing but regret.
Seeing the scene before him a faintly smug smile slowly spread across Luke’s face.
He couldn’t help but recall the past.
When he had first arrived in the Blackstone Highlands.
He had wandered through the territory several times.
Back then many of these very same merchants had crossed paths with him.
Yet not a single one had greeted him.
Some hadn’t even bothered to acknowledge his presence.
To them he had merely been the talentless hero.
An insignificant baron living in a remote territory.
But now...
Luke slowly swept his gaze across the hall.
One familiar face after another entered his sight.
He recognized quite a few of them.
The irony wasn’t lost on him.
The same people who had once ignored him.
Were now standing respectfully before him.
Smiling.
Greeting him with enthusiasm.
Treating him as someone worthy of their utmost respect.
’Heh... hypocrites.’ Luke shook his head inwardly.
Still he didn’t let those thoughts show on his face.
Maintaining a calm expression, he walked toward the elevated platform at the end of the hall.
Several broad marble steps led to a single seat reserved exclusively for the lord of the Blackstone Highlands.
His seat.
Step.
Step.
Step.
The sound of his footsteps echoed throughout the silent hall.
Reaching the top, Luke calmly turned around before taking his seat.
His gaze swept across the gathering below.
"You may all sit." His voice wasn’t loud.
Yet it carried enough authority for everyone to hear clearly.
"Thank you, Sir Luke."
One after another, the merchants bowed before taking their seats on the rows of chairs arranged neatly beneath the platform.
The previously tense atmosphere eased slightly.
Meanwhile...
Osric quietly walked toward the corner where the gifts had been placed.
Ignoring the curious looks directed at his bandaged appearance, he simply stood there with his hands behind his back.
Luke rested one arm on the throne’s armrest before slowly examining every face in the hall.
His eyes calmly moved from one merchant to another.
Experienced traders.
Young successors.
Representatives of merchant guilds.
Not a single expression escaped his notice.
Then.
His gaze paused for a brief moment.
Sophia.
A faint smile appeared on Luke’s face.
He gave her a small nod.
Sophia politely returned the gesture with a graceful smile before quietly lowering her head again.
Only then did Luke shift his attention back to the crowd.
"So..." He folded his hands together.
"For what reason has everyone gathered here today?" His calm question echoed across the hall.
The merchants collectively twitched.
’Sly bastard.’ Several of them cursed inwardly.
’As if he doesn’t already know why we’re here.’ Everyone understood perfectly well.
Luke was intentionally making them speak first.
That way whoever opened the negotiations would lose the initiative.
It was a classic bargaining tactic.
And they had all fallen into it.
For a few moments...
Silence lingered throughout the hall.
The merchants exchanged subtle glances, silently urging one another to take the first step.
Finally one middle-aged merchant slowly rose from his chair.
As soon as the merchant stood up.
Every gaze in the hall shifted toward him.
Luke’s blue eyes also settled on the man.
Despite becoming the center of attention.
The merchant remained completely composed.
Not even the slightest hint of nervousness appeared on his face.

His neatly combed white hair gave him a dignified appearance.
Several expensive rings adorned his fingers, each embedded with a different gemstone.
His luxurious robes were woven from high-quality fabric, while every accessory he wore silently proclaimed one thing—
Wealth.

chapters.title: Chapter 170: Baron Luke’s Petty Revenge?
paragraphs: The old merchant respectfully cupped his fists. "My greetings once again, Baron Luke."
Luke acknowledged him with a slight nod. "Go on."
A courteous smile appeared on the old man’s face.
"My name is Percival Langdon."
"I am a timber merchant."
"For more than five decades, my family has dealt in the transportation and trade of every kind of wood."
He calmly began listing them.
"Oak."
"Pine."
"Cedar."
"Exotic hardwoods."
"Lumber."
"And many other varieties."
Luke listened quietly, giving an occasional nod.
Meanwhile...
Several merchants seated nearby narrowed their eyes.
’Percival Langdon.’ They naturally recognized him.
The Langdon Family had operated in the timber trade for over fifty years.
Throughout the kingdom, they had earned an excellent reputation for both quality and reliability.
In the timber business. They were considered one of the established names.
Percival took a slow breath before revealing his true purpose.
"Sir Luke."
"I would like to establish a Branch within the Blackstone Highlands."
"If you are willing to permit it." The moment those words left his mouth—
The entire hall fell silent. Many merchants’ eyes widened.
Several even turned toward Percival in astonishment.
’A Branch?!’
’He isn’t here just to negotiate the toll fees?’
The hall stirred with whispers.
Several merchants exchanged puzzled looks. Some even frowned.
After all, Building a Branch inside another lord’s territory was no small decision.
It meant investing heavily in land, buildings, workers, and supplies.
More importantly...
It meant placing a significant portion of one’s business under someone else’s authority.
If relations ever turned hostile. Everything inside that Branch could be seized overnight.
And there would be very little the merchant could do about it. It was undoubtedly a risky gamble.
However...
The rewards were equally tempting.
A permanent Branch meant faster transportation. Safer storage. Direct access to Blackstone’s growing market.
And most importantly. It would earn Baron Luke’s goodwill.
With his Mid-Golden Knight combat power protecting the territory, caravans would no longer have to constantly fear attacks from bandits.
’Idiots.’
Percival caught the some mocking expressions directed at him. Several of them belonged to his longtime competitors.
Inwardly, he merely sneered.
’Keep laughing.’
’You’ll understand soon enough.’
Unlike the others. Percival had carefully observed the Blackstone Highlands.
For ten long years. The territory had remained almost unchanged.
Poor. Quiet. Almost forgotten.
Yet within merely fourteen days. Everything had transformed.
New construction projects appeared one after another. The population had increased.
The military had expanded at an unbelievable pace.
Trade had begun flourishing. The entire territory radiated vitality.
And all of it. Had happened because of a single person.
Percival slowly lifted his gaze toward the elevated throne.
There Baron Luke sat calmly.
A faint smile rested on his face as he looked back at him.
’This man...’
’He’s the reason behind all of it.’
That was precisely why Percival had made his decision.
He was willing to bet his family’s future on Luke.
After all for years, his caravans had suffered repeated attacks from bandit groups during transportation.
He wasn’t naive enough to believe those attacks were mere coincidence.
In fact...
He strongly suspected that several of his own business rivals had been secretly funding those bandits to weaken the Langdon Family’s trade.
If establishing a Branch in the Blackstone Highlands meant gaining Luke’s protection.
Then, in Percival’s eyes it was a gamble worth taking.
"I approve." Luke’s answer came without the slightest hesitation.
The moment those two words echoed through the hall. A huge smile of relief spread across Percival’s face.
He respectfully bowed. "Thank you, Baron Luke!"
Luke gave a slight nod before shifting his gaze across the entire gathering.
His expression gradually became serious.
"Now there’s something else I wish to announce."
Instantly every merchant straightened in their seats.
Luke calmly continued.
"As for the previous toll system." He paused for a brief moment.
"I am removing it."
A wave of confusion spread throughout the hall.
"Because I’m replacing it with a completely new one." His calm voice reached every corner of the room.
Immediately the merchants frowned. Whispers quietly spread among them.
’Why?’
’Is Baron Luke trying to squeeze more money from us?’
’Is this his way of getting back at us because we never supported Blackstone when it was struggling?’
’Are we about to pay for the mistakes of the previous merchants?’
Many expressions gradually turned ugly. Even several newly arrived merchants looked uneasy.
After all they hadn’t done anything wrong.
Yet now, they feared they would suffer the consequences of others past actions.
Still not a single person dared interrupt Luke.
Instead they quietly waited for him to finish.
Luke calmly rested one hand on the armrest of his chair. Then spoke again.
"From today onward. Every merchant caravan passing through the Blackstone Highlands."
"Will pay toll based on the total value of the goods they are transporting."
He deliberately added another sentence. "However small merchants are exempt from this rule."
The atmosphere immediately became even heavier. Still, everyone waited for the most important part.
*The price.*
Luke slowly swept his gaze across the hall.
Then he revealed the new toll rates.
TOLL TAX RATES
Category: Toll Rate | Goods Type
Essential Goods: 3% | Food, medicine, raw materials
Standard Goods: 5% | Tools, cloth, common trade items
Luxury Goods: 7% | Wine, jewelry, rare metals, exotic goods
Small Merchant (Low Value): 3 Silver | Local traders with low-value goods (per cart)
The moment the proposed rates were announced. The expressions of many merchants immediately darkened.
Their uneasy premonitions had seemingly come true.
’Baron Luke is being petty.’ That thought flashed through everyone minds.
Previously...
They had only needed to pay a fixed amount to cross the Blackstone Highlands.
The fee was predictable. Simple. Easy to calculate.
But now a percentage-based toll would directly scale with the value of their cargo.
For many merchants. That sounded far worse.
Whispers instantly spread throughout the hall.
"This is too much."
"My profits will shrink."
"How are we supposed to make money like this?"
Several merchants frowned deeply.
Others quietly began calculating the numbers in their heads.

chapters.title: Chapter 171: They’re All Fish | Reeling Them In Slowly
paragraphs: After all running a merchant caravan was never as simple as buying and selling goods.
They had to hire adventurers and mercenaries to escort the caravans.
Maintain wagons, horses, and equipment.
Pay salaries to their workers.
Provide compensation to the families of guards who died protecting the shipment.
Then there were the tons of "protection fees" demanded by bandit groups along the way.
And above all there was always the risk of losing everything.
If a caravan was ambushed. If valuable goods were stolen. Or if the cargo was destroyed during transport.
The merchant’s accumulated savings often became the only thing keeping their business alive.
Now if they also had to surrender a percentage of every shipment to Baron Luke. Their profit margins would undoubtedly shrink.
Especially for those dealing in luxury goods. Expensive silk. Rare gemstones. High-grade magic materials.
For them even a small percentage represented an huge amount of money.
Several luxury merchants exchanged anxious glances. Many had already decided to plead with Baron Luke to reconsider.
From his throne Luke silently observed the hall.
Merchants were whispering to one another with tense expressions.
Some were already preparing arguments. Others looked as though they wanted to stand up immediately.
Almost everyone present seemed dissatisfied.
His gaze briefly paused on Sophia. Even her usually composed expression had fallen.
Beside her Damien wore a similarly troubled look.
Even Percival’s confident expression faltered. ’Will I have to pay those rates as well?’
A trace of worry surfaced in his eyes.
After all he had only just requested permission to build a Branch.
If the new toll applied to him too, his expense would be increased.
Just then. Luke’s calm voice echoed across the hall once more.
"Before you make your judgment. I’d like to add something." His words instantly drew everyone’s attention.
The whispers gradually died away.
Within moments silence once again filled the grand hall.
Every pair of eyes turned toward Luke.
However this time, many of those gazes contained obvious dissatisfaction.
Some merchants had become so absorbed in calculating their losses that they had almost forgotten the young man sitting upon the throne possessed combat power comparable to a Mid-Golden Knight.
Luke noticed every expression.
Yet he didn’t mind in the slightest.
Instead a faint smile appeared on his lips.
’They’re all fish.’
’I just need to reel them in slowly.’
Without showing any impatience, he continued.
"First."
"I will construct watchtowers along the entire trade route passing through the Blackstone Highlands.
He paused deliberately.
"Each watchtower will be permanently manned by Bronze Knights."
"Twenty-four hours a day."
"They will ensure the safety of every merchant caravan passing through my territory."
The moment those words fell. The merchants’ expressions changed.
"What?"
"Bronze Knights?"
Several people widened their eyes in surprise.
Whispers immediately spread once again.
This single promise solved one of their greatest concerns.
The magical beasts.
As the Stormhowl Mountains stretched across the land like a colossal natural wall.
From the west all the way to the east.
They effectively separated the Northern Region from the southern lands.
The only alternative routes were to cross the monster-infested mountains.
Or venture through the endless forests surrounding them.
Both options were notoriously dangerous.
Fortunately the Blackstone Highlands occupied one of the safest sections of the mountain range.
Compared to other areas the monster population there was remarkably low.
Its rocky terrain and lack of dense vegetation made it unsuitable for most magical beasts to establish nests.
Because of that over the years, merchants had gradually carved out a narrow trade road through the region.
Although the route was considerably longer.
It remained the safest land passage connecting the Northern Region with the eastern, western, and southern territories.
That single road had become the lifeline of countless merchant caravans.
However. Safe. Didn’t mean completely secure.
Blackstone stood near the eastern edge of the Stormhowl Mountains.
From time to time, magical beasts descended from the upper mountain slopes. While others emerged from the forests below.
Whenever they encountered merchant caravans. Attacks were almost inevitable.
Many guards had lost their lives defending shipments. Numerous caravans had been destroyed.
And countless fortunes had vanished into the jaws of magical beasts. The losses accumulated year after year.
So if Baron Luke truly eliminated that problem. Then the merchants would not only save enormous amounts of money.
They would also gain something even more valuable.
Peace of mind.
Luke’s smile remained calm as he looked across the hall.
Then, he continued.
"Second, I will eliminate every bandit operating within my territory." His firm voice echoed throughout the hall.
A few merchants couldn’t help but straighten in their seats.
Luke continued before anyone could interrupt.
"I will also improve the roads."
"The routes will be widened and reinforced for long-distance travel."
"So even during heavy rain you won’t have to worry about the roads turning into mud or becoming impassable."
The merchants looked at one another.
Several of them had personally experienced wagons getting stuck in muddy roads for days.
That promise alone was worth a great deal.
Luke raised another finger.
"Furthermore..."
"Silver Knight patrols will regularly travel along the trade route."
"If any merchant caravan sends out an emergency signal."
"They will respond as quickly as possible."
The hall grew noticeably quieter.
Silver Knights.
Not Bronze Knights.
That meant an even higher level of protection.
Luke wasn’t finished.
"For merchants who frequently use the Blackstone Highlands."
"I’ll introduce a discount system."
He gestured toward Osric.
The latter stepped forward and unfurled a large parchment.
A neatly organized table was displayed for everyone to see.
Luke calmly explained it.
DISCOUNTS
Scenario : Discount
Return Trip (Within 7 Days) : 50% Off
Bulk Caravan (10+ Carts) : 10% Off
Loyal Merchants (Monthly Pass) : 20% Off
Essential Goods (Food, Medicine) : Lower Toll Rate (3%)
Murmurs immediately spread throughout the hall. Many merchants instinctively began calculating the savings in their minds.
Luke allowed them a few moments before speaking again.
"And that’s not all."
"I will establish multiple Safe Zones along the trade route."
His words immediately drew everyone’s attention back to him.
