Luke allowed them a few moments before speaking again.
"And that’s not all."
"I will establish multiple Safe Zones along the trade route."
His words immediately drew everyone’s attention back to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 172: The First Step to a Trade Empire
paragraphs: "Each Safe Zone will be permanently guarded by Silver Knights."
"There merchant caravans may safely rest."
"Repair wagons."
"Resupply daily necessities."
"And spend the night without constantly worrying about beast attacks."
As Luke finished speaking.
The atmosphere inside the hall changed completely.
The expressions of the merchants gradually changed.
One after another. The frowns on their faces disappeared.
Because they suddenly realized something.
Baron Luke hadn’t merely introduced a new toll system.
He had practically solved almost every problem they faced during transportation.
Security. Safer roads. Emergency support. Resting points. Food and daily supplies. Protected Safe Zones.
Even loyalty discounts for frequent merchants.
Every single point struck directly at the difficulties they had endured for years.
Then Luke casually added another condition.
"Oh, right."
"If any merchant requires additional protection."
"You may also hire soldiers from the Blackstone Highlands as escorts."
That single sentence instantly attracted everyone’s attention.
"Of course." Luke raised a finger.
"The escort service isn’t free. There will be separate charges."
"And due to military requirements. Only Bronze Knights and soldiers below that level will be available."
"Even then it will depend on their availability."
No one complained. On the contrary. Many merchants eyes lit up.
Even Bronze Knights were considered elite escorts.
Compared to ordinary mercenaries. Their discipline and combat strength were on an entirely different level.
By now no one felt the new toll system was expensive anymore.
Instead many began calculating how much money they would actually save.
Fewer beast attacks. Reduced escort expenses. Safer roads. Lower cargo losses. Faster travel.
In the long run. The overall profits would likely increase instead of decrease.
Then another thought surfaced in many minds.
’Should we establish a Branch here as well?’
With the loyalty discounts and a permanently protected trade route. And a lord who possess Mid-Golden Knight combat power.
The Blackstone Highlands suddenly appeared to be one of the safest commercial locations in the nearest region.
The only condition was remaining on Baron Luke’s good side.
No one wished to imagine the consequences of becoming his enemy.
For a brief moment, Silence filled the hall.
Then—
A merchant suddenly stood up.
"Sir Luke!"
"I agree!"
Another immediately rose.
"Me too!"
"And, Sir Luke"
"I would also like permission to build a Branch within the Blackstone Highlands!"
Before Luke could even respond. A third merchant hurriedly stood.
"My family wishes to establish one as well!"
"Please approve our request!"
"I also want to lease land!"
"Our merchant guild is interested too!"
One after another. Excited voices erupted throughout the hall.
Merchants who had looked dissatisfied only moments earlier were now eagerly volunteering.
Several even began speaking over one another.
Their expressions were filled with urgency.
Because everyone understood the same thing.
Whoever secured a Branch first. Would gain the greatest advantage.
If they hesitated now. Then their competitors would seize the opportunity instead.
Seeing the enthusiastic reactions a satisfied smile appeared on Luke’s face.
He lightly waved his hand.
"Record their names."
"Yes, My Lord."
The maids immediately bowed before hurrying through the hall with parchment and quills in hand.
One after another. The merchants eagerly reported their names, afraid someone else would secure a better location before they did.
Luke quietly watched the lively scene.
He wasn’t the least bit worried about running out of land for Branchs.
After all this was only the beginning.
’Soon.’
’The Blackstone Highlands will expand toward the Stormhowl Mountains.’
There would be more than enough space.
His thoughts naturally drifted elsewhere. ’And I still have to deal with the western border.’
Luke recalled the soldiers stationed there.
Even one of the territory’s former Silver Knights was still guarding that region.
Normally the western border wasn’t considered particularly dangerous.
The Stormhowl Mountains acted as a colossal natural barrier between the Blackstone Highlands and the Demi-Human Empire.
The distance separating the two was enormous.
Hundreds of mountain peaks, deep valleys, and monster-infested forests lay between them.
It was a nightmare for any large army to march through.
Because of that for many years, neither side had paid much attention to that frontier.
However everything had changed after the Demon War years ago.
Numerous demi-human tribes had begun appearing within the western mountain ranges.
Their movements had become increasingly frequent. Although no major conflict had erupted.
Their growing activity was enough to concern the territory.
That was precisely why Lady Sepharina—
Aurielle’s mother—
Had permanently stationed troops along the western border. Their purpose wasn’t to wage war.
It was to observe. And to ensure that, should anything unexpected happen.
The Blackstone Highlands would not be caught unprepared.
Luke silently stored the matter away in his mind.
He would have to inspect that border personally sooner or later.
But that could wait.
Then his attention returned to the hall. The merchants were still speaking over one another.
Some were even trying to push forward to register their names first.
The entire hall had become surprisingly noisy.
Luke slowly raised one hand.
"Quiet."
Instantly the bustling hall fell silent.
Every merchant immediately closed their mouth.
Hundreds of eyes turned toward the young baron seated upon the elevated throne, waiting for his next words.
Luke gave a small nod. After ensuring everyone’s attention was on him.
He decided to reveal the next part of the plan he had prepared ever since obtaining the Mana Well and the Healing Spring.
Without saying a word. Luke waved his hand.
A faint flash of light appeared. And two transparent crystal vials materialized in his palm.
One contained a clear blue liquid.
The other shimmered with a gentle emerald-green glow.
The moment they appeared. Every merchant’s gaze was instantly drawn toward them.
Luke calmly raised both vials.
"The blue potion." He lifted it slightly. "is a Mana Recovery Potion."
Then he raised the green one. "And this is a Healing Potion."
He briefly explained their effects.
The blue potion rapidly restored consumed aether or mana.
While the green potion accelerated the healing of wounds and significantly shortened recovery time.
The moment those descriptions reached the merchants ears. Their eyes lit up.

chapters.title: Chapter 173: The Jealous Females
paragraphs: Almost simultaneously. Their merchant instincts immediately kicked in.
’A new product!’
’No... two new products!’
’How much could these sell for?’
’How difficult are they to produce?’
’Can we secure exclusive trading rights?’
Hundreds of calculations flashed through their minds within seconds.
Seeing those greedy, sparkling eyes. A broad grin slowly spread across Luke’s face.
He had been waiting for exactly this reaction.
Then he casually added,
"These potions are effective for Iron Knights and below."
A brief pause followed.
"And for mages. They are effective up to the Apprentice Mage Realm."
The entire hall erupted into commotion.
"What?!"
"Iron Knight level?!"
Several merchants nearly stood up from their seats.
Their breathing became noticeably heavier.
They understood the significance of those words far better than ordinary people.
After all once a person stepped beyond the Body Temper Realm. The largest cultivation market belonged to Iron Knights.
Knight cultivation was straightforward.
As long as one possessed enough resources and perseverance.
Almost anyone could embark on that path.
Because of that the overwhelming majority of human cultivators eventually became Iron Knights.
The market demand was enormous.
The Mage path, however was completely different.
Without an innate affinity for mana or exceptional magical talent. Becoming a mage was nearly impossible.
As a result the number of mages was only a tiny fraction of the knight population.
Even so potions capable of restoring mana for Apprentice Mages still possessed tremendous commercial value.
Luke calmly looked across the hall before making the next announcement.
"Starting tomorrow the Blackstone Highlands will officially begin selling both of these potions."
The merchants immediately straightened in their seats.
Luke calmly continued. "However, There will be purchase limits."
He raised one finger.
"Each merchant group may purchase only one hundred Healing Potions and one hundred Mana Potions.
Then he added another condition. "As for individual buyers."
"The limit will be ten bottles of each potion per person."
The hall immediately became quiet.
Luke wasn’t finished yet.
"This restriction will remain in effect for one week."
"After that the purchase limit will gradually increase."
"Until then those are the maximum quantities anyone may buy."
The excitement that had filled the hall only moments earlier instantly cooled.
Many merchants expressions fell. Some even sighed.
Although Baron Luke hadn’t mentioned the price yet. They already understood the implication.
With such strict purchase limits. Their profit margins on each trading trip would be much lower than expected.
Especially because the purchase quota had been fixed. until the next phase of Luke’s sales plan began.
Whispers quietly spread throughout the hall.
"Only one hundred?"
"That’s far too few."
"How are we supposed to satisfy our customers?"
"This quantity won’t even last a single city."
Several merchants looked genuinely disappointed.
From his throne. Luke silently observed every reaction.
Naturally he noticed their gloomy expressions.
Yet...
He didn’t change his decision. Nor did he offer any explanation.
It wasn’t because he lacked stock.
On the contrary he possessed an enormous reserve of both potions.
Far more than these merchants could imagine.
So...
Why impose such strict limits?
The answer was simple.
Luke wasn’t merely planning to sell potions. He was building a brand.
Very soon the Blackstone Store would officially open.
And before flooding the market with supply. He first wanted to create demand.
Scarcity would make the potions the talk of every city.
Merchants would compete for them. Customers would ask about them.
Rumors would spread from caravan to caravan.
By the time the purchase limits were relaxed. The name Blackstone would already have reached the ears of countless people across the kingdom.
Luke’s objective was never simply to sell potions. He wanted to create something far more valuable.
A reputation. A legend. A potion that possessed no side effects. No potion toxicity.
And could only be purchased within the Blackstone Highlands.
That exclusivity alone would become its greatest advertisement.
Once word spread adventurers, hundreds of, thousands of knights, mages, and merchant caravans would travel to Blackstone just to obtain those potions.
With them would come craftsmen. Talented individuals. Investors. And thousands of opportunities.
The territory’s fame would naturally spread throughout the kingdom.
And Luke knew this was only the beginning.
In the future the system would undoubtedly reward him with even more extraordinary items.
When that happened. The Blackstone Store would already possess a renowned reputation.
Eventually he could even establish branches in other territories.
That was his long-term plan. After the meeting concluded.
One after another, they respectfully bowed.
"Thank you, Baron Luke."
"We’ll take our leave."
Soon...
The grand hall gradually emptied as merchant groups departed one by one.
However two people remained seated. Sophia. And her elder brother, Damien.
Seeing this several merchants glanced back before leaving.
Envious expressions appeared on many faces.
’The Blackriver Merchant Family daughter really knows how to win Baron Luke’s heart.’
That very thought surfaced in the minds of nearly everyone present.
Some merchants sighed inwardly. Others secretly regretted not sending their own sons or daughters to build a relationship with the young baron sooner.
Meanwhile several young men looked toward Luke with obvious jealousy.
After all the Hero Luke was becoming increasingly famous.
His strength continued to rise. His territory was flourishing. His influence was expanding.
And now even one outstanding beauty after another seemed drawn toward him.
To them it was enough to make anyone envious.
While the younger female merchants. Especially those from influential merchant families.
Couldn’t help but cast jealous glances toward Sophia.
After all each of them had dressed meticulously for today’s meeting.
Elegant gowns hugged their graceful figures.
Luxurious fabrics shimmered under the sunlight.
Some dresses even revealed a tasteful glimpse of their shoulders or collarbones, subtly highlighting their beauty without crossing the bounds of nobility.
Before coming here quite a few of them had secretly hoped to leave a favorable impression on Baron Luke.
Yet throughout the entire meeting. Luke hadn’t spared them even a second glance.
Not even once.
That realization left many of them feeling secretly defeated.
’Is Lady Sophia really that much prettier than us?’

chapters.title: Chapter 174: Sophia’s Shy Confession
paragraphs: ’Or does Baron Luke simply have no interest on us?’
Some quietly bit their lips. Others looked toward Sophia with obvious envy.
If Luke had known what they were thinking. He would have laughed bitterly.
’Girls...’
’You should be thankful that my wife wasn’t attending today’s meeting.’
’Otherwise... none of you would’ve even dared wear dresses showing that much skin.’
Just imagining his wife’s icy smile. Luke felt a chill run down his spine.
Fortunately she had chosen to leave earlier.
Otherwise today’s merchant meeting would’ve turned into an entirely different battlefield.
Soon the last merchant departed.
The once-crowded hall gradually became quiet. Only two guests remained seated.
Sophia. And her elder brother, Damien.
Luke looked toward them with a warm smile.
"Lady Sophia."
"It’s been a while."
"How have you been?"
Sophia gracefully rose from her seat.
Holding the sides of her dress, she offered Luke a courteous noble bow.
Beside her Damien respectfully did the same.
A gentle smile bloomed across Sophia’s beautiful face.
"I’ve been doing well, Sir Luke."
"I hope you’ve been well too."
Luke smiled and nodded.
"I have."
Sophia then turned slightly toward the man beside her.
"Allow me to formally introduce him."
"My elder brother Damien Blackriver."
Damien stepped forward and respectfully cupped his fists.
"It is an honor to finally meet you properly, Baron Luke."
Luke returned the greeting with a slight nod.
"The pleasure is mine."
After the brief introductions. Sophia exchanged a glance with Damien.
Both of them seemed to have already reached a decision before coming here.
Taking a small breath. Sophia looked directly into Luke’s eyes.
"Sir Luke."
Sophia took a slow breath before revealing the purpose of today’s visit.
"Our family has reached a decision."
Luke quietly listened.
"The Blackriver Family has decided to relocate to the Blackstone Highlands."
"We also intend to move our entire wine processing facility here."
The moment those words were spoken.
Even Osric, who had been silently standing nearby, looked over in surprise.
Relocate the entire processing plant?
That wasn’t a decision any merchant family could make lightly.
Luke, however, remained calm. While a faint smile appeared on his face.
He had expected something similar.
After all...
The moment Sophia reported that he had defeated a Mid-Golden Knight, the Blackriver Family would naturally realize where the future lay.
Rather than waiting until every valuable piece of land had been claimed.
It was far wiser to secure their place now.
’A wise decision.’ Luke nodded inwardly.
The Blackriver Family’s greatest business was their famous grapes.
Not only did they cultivate rare varieties. They also refined them into high-quality wines that were sold throughout the kingdom.
Relocating that entire operation. Would be a massive undertaking.
Naturally it also came with serious problems.
Fresh grapes spoiled quickly after being harvested.
If they weren’t processed in time. The quality of the wine would decrease dramatically.
Fortunately the Blackriver Family had already prepared a solution.
Sophia calmly explained,
"We’ve already discussed this issue."
"We plan to purchase specialized liquid storage bags from the Ocean Territory."
"They can store enormous amounts of liquid safely."
"Instead of transporting fresh grapes."
"We’ll squeeze the juice at the vineyard first. Then transport the juice here for processing."
Luke nodded in understanding. That was indeed a practical solution.
Although it still wasn’t perfect.
If large-capacity Spatial Rings were affordable. None of these problems would even exist.
Unfortunately those treasures were expensive.
Especially rings capable of storing large quantities of goods.
Even wealthy merchant families found them difficult to acquire.
Otherwise every major caravan would have been transporting cargo inside Spatial Rings instead of wagons.
Another reason merchants rarely used large Spatial Rings for transportation was security.
If a caravan carrying ordinary wagons was ambushed. The bandits still had to seize each wagon individually.
Many times, the merchants could at least save part of their cargo.
But a Spatial Ring was different. If the person wearing it was killed first.
The entire shipment would instantly fall into the enemy’s hands.
Years of investment gone in a single battle.
That risk was simply too great.
Moreover merchants trusted very few people.
Entrusting a Spatial Ring worth a fortune to someone else was almost unthinkable.
What if the carrier fled?
What if they secretly stole the goods? Or simply disappeared?
Because of those concerns, most merchant families gradually abandoned the idea of transporting goods inside large Spatial Rings.
Instead...
They only carried small Spatial Pouches for storing money, important documents, and a handful of precious items.
Then Luke leaned back slightly, silently weighing the benefits.
If the Blackriver Family truly relocated. His territory would gain tons of advantages.
New jobs would be created for the local population. Blackstone’s reputation would rise even further.
The economy would grow rapidly.
And the guards and knights employed by the Blackriver Family would, in practice, become another defensive force within his territory.
Of course that cooperation would only continue as long as Luke remained powerful enough to command respect.
Strength...
Was the foundation of everything.
So just as Luke was about to nod in agreement.
Sophia hesitated. She gently clasped her hands together.
"However" Her voice became noticeably softer.
Then she slowly lowered her head.
Her cheeks gradually flushed a delicate shade of pink.
The image resembled a young noble maiden. Shyly preparing to speak before her future husband.
That sight alone.
Immediately made Luke’s instincts scream.
’Why do I suddenly have a bad feeling about this?’
Damien had expected this moment.
Still seeing his younger sister’s behavior, he couldn’t help but roll his eyes.
’She was so confident before entering the hall.’
’Where did all that confidence go?’
He sighed inwardly. However, wisely kept his mouth shut.
This wasn’t the time to interrupt.
Sophia nervously clenched the edge of her dress.
Her heartbeat echoed loudly in her ears.
"L-Luke..."
She took a deep breath.
Gathering every ounce of courage she possessed.
She finally spoke.
"I-I wants to... ma-marry you..."
"...and become your concubine."
The words barely escaped her lips.
Her face instantly turned crimson.
Slowly.
Very slowly.
She lifted her head.

’Otherwise... none of you would’ve even dared wear dresses showing that much skin.’
Just imagining his wife’s icy smile.
Luke felt a chill run down his spine.
Fortunately she had chosen to leave earlier.
Otherwise today’s merchant meeting would’ve turned into an entirely different battlefield.
Soon the last merchant departed.
The once-crowded hall gradually became quiet.
Only two guests remained seated.
Sophia.
And her elder brother, Damien.
Luke looked toward them with a warm smile.
"Lady Sophia."
"It’s been a while."
"How have you been?"
Sophia gracefully rose from her seat.
Holding the sides of her dress, she offered Luke a courteous noble bow.
Beside her Damien respectfully did the same.
A gentle smile bloomed across Sophia’s beautiful face.
"I’ve been doing well, Sir Luke."
"I hope you’ve been well too."
Luke smiled and nodded.
"I have."
Sophia then turned slightly toward the man beside her.
"Allow me to formally introduce him."
"My elder brother Damien Blackriver."
Damien stepped forward and respectfully cupped his fists.
"It is an honor to finally meet you properly, Baron Luke."
Luke returned the greeting with a slight nod.
"The pleasure is mine."
After the brief introductions.
Sophia exchanged a glance with Damien.
Both of them seemed to have already reached a decision before coming here.
Taking a small breath.
Sophia looked directly into Luke’s eyes.
"Sir Luke."
Sophia took a slow breath before revealing the purpose of today’s visit.
"Our family has reached a decision."
Luke quietly listened.
"The Blackriver Family has decided to relocate to the Blackstone Highlands."
"We also intend to move our entire wine processing facility here."
The moment those words were spoken.
Even Osric, who had been silently standing nearby, looked over in surprise.
Relocate the entire processing plant?
That wasn’t a decision any merchant family could make lightly.
Luke, however, remained calm.
While a faint smile appeared on his face.
He had expected something similar.
After all...
The moment Sophia reported that he had defeated a Mid-Golden Knight, the Blackriver Family would naturally realize where the future lay.
Rather than waiting until every valuable piece of land had been claimed.
It was far wiser to secure their place now.
’A wise decision.’ Luke nodded inwardly.
The Blackriver Family’s greatest business was their famous grapes.
Not only did they cultivate rare varieties.
They also refined them into high-quality wines that were sold throughout the kingdom.
Relocating that entire operation.
Would be a massive undertaking.
Naturally it also came with serious problems.
Fresh grapes spoiled quickly after being harvested.
If they weren’t processed in time.
The quality of the wine would decrease dramatically.
Fortunately the Blackriver Family had already prepared a solution.
Sophia calmly explained,
"We’ve already discussed this issue."
"We plan to purchase specialized liquid storage bags from the Ocean Territory."
"They can store enormous amounts of liquid safely."
"Instead of transporting fresh grapes."
"We’ll squeeze the juice at the vineyard first.
Then transport the juice here for processing."
Luke nodded in understanding.
That was indeed a practical solution.
Although it still wasn’t perfect.
If large-capacity Spatial Rings were affordable.
None of these problems would even exist.
Unfortunately those treasures were expensive.
Especially rings capable of storing large quantities of goods.
Even wealthy merchant families found them difficult to acquire.
Otherwise every major caravan would have been transporting cargo inside Spatial Rings instead of wagons.
Another reason merchants rarely used large Spatial Rings for transportation was security.
If a caravan carrying ordinary wagons was ambushed.
The bandits still had to seize each wagon individually.
Many times, the merchants could at least save part of their cargo.
But a Spatial Ring was different.
If the person wearing it was killed first.
The entire shipment would instantly fall into the enemy’s hands.
Years of investment gone in a single battle.
That risk was simply too great.
Moreover merchants trusted very few people.
Entrusting a Spatial Ring worth a fortune to someone else was almost unthinkable.
What if the carrier fled?
What if they secretly stole the goods?
Or simply disappeared?
Because of those concerns, most merchant families gradually abandoned the idea of transporting goods inside large Spatial Rings.
Instead...
They only carried small Spatial Pouches for storing money, important documents, and a handful of precious items.
Then Luke leaned back slightly, silently weighing the benefits.
If the Blackriver Family truly relocated.
His territory would gain tons of advantages.
New jobs would be created for the local population.
Blackstone’s reputation would rise even further.
The economy would grow rapidly.
And the guards and knights employed by the Blackriver Family would, in practice, become another defensive force within his territory.
Of course that cooperation would only continue as long as Luke remained powerful enough to command respect.
Strength...
Was the foundation of everything.
So just as Luke was about to nod in agreement.
Sophia hesitated.
She gently clasped her hands together.
"However" Her voice became noticeably softer.
Then she slowly lowered her head.
Her cheeks gradually flushed a delicate shade of pink.
The image resembled a young noble maiden.
Shyly preparing to speak before her future husband.
That sight alone.
Immediately made Luke’s instincts scream.
’Why do I suddenly have a bad feeling about this?’
Damien had expected this moment.
Still seeing his younger sister’s behavior, he couldn’t help but roll his eyes.
’She was so confident before entering the hall.’
’Where did all that confidence go?’
He sighed inwardly.
However, wisely kept his mouth shut.
This wasn’t the time to interrupt.
Sophia nervously clenched the edge of her dress.
Her heartbeat echoed loudly in her ears.
"L-Luke..."
She took a deep breath.
Gathering every ounce of courage she possessed.
She finally spoke.
"I-I wants to... ma-marry you..."
"...and become your concubine."
The words barely escaped her lips.
Her face instantly turned crimson.
Slowly.
Very slowly.
She lifted her head.

chapters.title: Chapter 175: The System’s Terrible Advice
paragraphs: One eye remained tightly shut from embarrassment, while the other cautiously peeked toward Luke.
She secretly waited for his reaction.
After all.
She had always been praised for her beauty. Among noble ladies.
She was considered exceptional. Even the daughters of many barons couldn’t compare with her appearance.
Surely Baron Luke would at least look pleasantly surprised.
But...
The expression she saw.
Wasn’t happiness. Nor excitement. Nor even embarrassment.
Instead Luke was cautiously looking around the entire hall.
Left. Right. Behind the pillars. Toward the entrance. Even toward the ceiling.
His eyes darted everywhere with astonishing vigilance.
Sophia blinked.
’What... is Sir Luke looking for?’ She followed his gaze around the room.
Nothing. There was absolutely nothing unusual.
Damien looked equally confused.
’Did someone enter?’
Even Osric, who had been standing motionless beside the mountain of gifts like a genuine mummy.
Nearly jumped out of his bandages.
"W-What?!" His eyes widened beneath the wrappings.
Then almost instinctively. He quietly shuffled behind the pile of gift boxes, using them as cover.
’Nope.’
’I’m not getting involved in this.’
’Not after what Lady Aurielle did to me.’
Meanwhile...
Luke continued scanning every corner of the hall. Several tense seconds passed.
Nothing happened. No familiar voice. No terrifying sword. No sudden appearance.
Only then Luke slowly let out a long breath.
"Phew..."
He pressed a hand against his chest.
’Thank the heavens.’
’Aurielle isn’t here.’ Relief washed over him.
Somehow his wife had an almost supernatural ability to appear at the worst possible moments.
Especially whenever another woman said something remotely dangerous.
More than once, she had seemingly materialized out of thin air.
To the point where Luke had begun questioning whether she possessed some hidden teleportation ability.
So after a few moments later, just as Luke was about to politely refuse her proposal—
Accepting only the Blackriver Family’s alliance and business partnership—
The system suddenly spoke.
[Heh... And you still call yourself a man?]
[The Hero Luke?]
[A beautiful woman willingly offers to warm your bed.]
[And you’re actually thinking of refusing?]
Luke’s mouth immediately twitched.
’Easy for you to say.’
’It’s not your balls that are constantly in danger.’
He shot back inwardly without hesitation.
The memory of Aurielle’s purple sword flashed through his mind.
His body instinctively shivered.
The system fell silent for a brief moment.
Then it spoke again.
[Luke...]
[Look at her.]
Luke subconsciously raised his head.
His blue eyes met Sophia’s. She stood there quietly.
Her delicate fingers nervously twisted the corner of her dress.
Her cheeks were still crimson.
Despite her embarrassment. She hadn’t withdrawn her words.
Instead she looked at him with a mixture of hope. Anxiety. And expectation.
Luke couldn’t deny it. She was beautiful almost compare to Margaret.
More importantly. Those hopeful eyes carried genuine sincerity.
The system continued in a quieter tone.
[If you reject her.]
[Have you thought about how heartbroken she’ll be?]
Luke’s expression slowly became complicated.
He knew the first person someone truly fell for. Often left the deepest mark on the heart.
Whether it became a cherished memory.
Or a lifelong regret.
It rarely disappeared completely.
Even years later. Even after finding someone else. That scar often remained.
A silent reminder of what could never be.
The system’s voice echoed once more.
[That’s why.]
[I can’t let you become a demon.]
[A cold...]
[Heartless demon!]
Luke’s eyebrow twitched violently.
’Since when did refusing a marriage proposal make someone a heartless demon?’
He couldn’t help but complain inwardly.
The system’s logic was becoming stranger by the day.
[So marry her Luke and fck her. (ง •̀_•́)ง Do it.]
Luke narrowed his eyes. ’So it’s all about Fcking again.’
The system screen flickered.
Bzzt.
For a brief second. The emoji froze.
Then silence. Not a single reply came.
Luke could almost imagine the system pretending it hadn’t been exposed.
"Sigh." A helpless sigh escaped his lips.
This situation was far more troublesome than dealing with merchants.
He didn’t want to marry another woman. Not because Sophia wasn’t beautiful.
She undoubtedly was. But because he already had five wives.
And if someday in the future. He truly considered another marriage. He would first have to seek their opinions.
Knowing Aurielle alone. Luke could already imagine the answer.
’Absolutely not.’
No...
He had to resolve this carefully. Without hurting Sophia’s maiden heart.
Luke gently called out,
"Sophia."
Hearing her name spoken so softly. Sophia immediately raised her head.
Her nervousness seemed to vanish for an instant.
Those beautiful eyes sparkled with anticipation as they met Luke’s.
Beside her Damien unconsciously held his breath. His heart began pounding.
After all if this marriage truly happened. The Blackriver Merchant Family’s status would soar overnight.
Becoming connected to Hero Luke by marriage. Would elevate their influence throughout the kingdom.
The atmosphere became incredibly quiet.
Luke smiled gently. "As for your family’s earlier proposal."
"I accept it."
A look of joy immediately appeared on Sophia’s face.
"The relocation of the Blackriver Family."
"And the construction of your processing plant."
"You have my approval."
"If you encounter any difficulties during the relocation."
"You may inform me."
"As long as it’s within my ability."
"I’ll provide my full support."
Sophia’s smile became even brighter.
"Thank you, Sir Luke."
She respectfully bowed.
Yet she didn’t move.
Instead she quietly looked back at Luke.
Her heart knew, that wasn’t the answer she had truly been hoping for.
Luke noticed it. Damien noticed it as well.
"And as for marriage..."
Luke paused for a brief moment before smiling apologetically.
"I’m not planning to marry anyone else."
"I already have five wives."
The words landed softly. Yet they carried considerable weight.
Sophia’s hopeful smile froze.
Her bright eyes gradually dimmed.
A faint ache spread through her chest. It wasn’t unbearable. But it was enough to make her lower her gaze.
Even Damien silently sighed.
’As expected.’ It had always been a difficult possibility.
However before the atmosphere could completely sink—
Luke spoke again.
"Though..."
"I don’t know what the future holds."
His words made Sophia’s eyelashes tremble. She instinctively looked back at him.

chapters.title: Chapter 176: Maids Holding Their Skirts.
paragraphs: Luke merely smiled. It wasn’t a promise. Nor was it a rejection.
Simply.
A vague answer. An uncertain future.
In Luke’s mind. This was the gentlest solution he could think of.
Perhaps she would wait for a few months.
Maybe even a few years. Then, as time passed. She would naturally meet someone she truly loved.
Someone who could remain by her side.
That way she wouldn’t have to suffer the pain of a direct rejection.
Sometimes hope faded more gently than heartbreak.
At least that was what Luke believed.
However the moment those words reached Sophia’s ears—
The tiny flame that had almost gone out. Quietly ignited once more.
A faint sparkle returned to her beautiful eyes.
’I’ll wait.’ She silently clenched her hands.
’No matter how long it takes.’
’Even if it’s ten years.’
’Or twenty.’
’I’ll wait for you.’
That silent resolve settled deep within her heart.
She herself couldn’t explain why she had fallen for Luke.
If someone had asked. She probably wouldn’t have been able to give a clear answer.
Perhaps.
It was because he had protected her from bandits, without asking for anything in return.
Perhaps.
It was because he always treated her with kindness and respect.
Or perhaps.
It was because, unlike so many noblemen she had met before.
When Luke looked at her. His eyes weren’t clouded with greed or lust.
He simply saw Sophia.
And somehow that had been enough for her heart to quietly choose him.
’I’ll wait for you.’ Sophia silently made another promise to herself.
’And one day, I’ll make you fall in love with me.’
If Luke had somehow heard that thought. He would’ve instantly buried his face in his hands.
’One Aurora is already enough.’
’If another woman starts chasing me like this.’
’I honestly don’t know how Aurielle is going to kill me tomorrow.’
After exchanging a few final words.
Sophia and Damien respectfully bowed before leaving the hall together.
The huge doors slowly closed behind them.
Creak.
Silence returned once again. Luke leaned back against his chair.
"Sigh."
A long, weary sigh escaped his lips. Dealing with Sophia.
Surprisingly.
Had been even more mentally exhausting than fighting enemies.
He rubbed the bridge of his nose before standing up.
Turning toward the bandaged "mummy" nearby, he said,
"Osric.
"My Lord."
"I’m heading outside to deploy the watchtowers."
"Send the knight archers to each location as soon as they leave the territory."
"We’ll station them immediately."
Osric respectfully lowered his head.
"As you command, My Lord."
Luke gave a slight nod.
Without wasting another moment. He strode out of the hall. His footsteps gradually faded into the distance.
Tap. Tap. Tap. Until...
Silence remained.
Osric quietly watched Luke’s departing figure. For a long while. He didn’t move.
Then, his eyes gradually became moist.
A faint smile filled with both pride and nostalgia appeared beneath the bandages.
He softly muttered to himself,
"Lady Sepharina."
"If only you were here."
"You would have been so happy to witness this."
His voice trembled ever so slightly.
For years, he had watched the Blackstone Highlands slowly decline.
He had witnessed countless hardships.
Countless disappointments.
Yet today again, he could see a future that was rapidly taking shape before his very eyes.
Looking toward the hall’s entrance where Luke had disappeared.
Osric smiled.
"The territory has finally found its wings."
A pair of wings.
Named Luke.
And with those wings the Blackstone Highlands would no longer remain trapped beneath the mountains.
One day it would soar proudly into the sky.
"Ahh." Luke closed his eyes for a brief moment and drew in a deep breath.
"Fresh air." A relaxed smile appeared on his face.
The merchant meeting had lasted for several hours.
Without him realizing it. Morning had quietly slipped away.
Now the warm afternoon sunlight bathed the Blackstone Highlands.
Leaving the mansion behind. Luke stepped into the spacious courtyard.
The guards and maids standing nearby respectfully greeted him.
"Greetings, My Lord!"
Luke returned their greetings with a nod.
Then without another word. He activated the first form of the Faceless Titan.
A faint silver glow rippled across his body.
Immediately afterward. He used Form Assimilation.
A low humming sound echoed around him.
Vmmm.
The silver light behind his back suddenly intensified.
The next instant—
FWOOOSH!!
Two enormous silver wings burst from Luke’s back. Each feather gleamed like polished metal beneath the afternoon sun.
With an impressive wingspan of nearly fifteen feet. The majestic wings spread proudly behind him.
The surrounding guards froze.
"What?!"
"W-Wings?!"
Several maids instinctively covered their mouths in shock.
For a split second. The courtyard fell into complete silence.
However the surprise lasted only an instant.
The moment they recognized the familiar figure standing beneath those magnificent wings.
Everyone immediately relaxed.
"It’s Lord Luke."
"I almost had a heart attack." One knight let out a helpless laugh.
Another guard smiled proudly. "As expected of our Lord."
The maids also giggled among themselves, their earlier shock quickly turning into admiration.
"So beautiful."
"They’re shining."
Luke simply smiled at everyone’s reactions.
Then he bent his knees slightly.
His enormous silver wings slowly stretched to their full length.
Fwoooosh Power gathered beneath them. The surrounding air visibly stirred.
Luke looked toward the distant sky.
"Let’s go."
BOOM!!
With a single powerful flap—
The gigantic wings unleashed a violent blast of wind.
Dust exploded outward. Leaves danced wildly through the air.
The force alone sent powerful gusts sweeping across the courtyard.
"My skirt!"
"Kyaa!"
The nearby maids immediately cried out in surprise. Their dresses fluttered violently in the sudden wind.
Blushing bright red.
They hurriedly grabbed their skirts with both hands before they could fly any higher.
Some squatted instinctively. Others turned sideways to shield themselves.
"W-Wait...!"
"Hold it!"
Meanwhile.
"S-So white." A few young knights stared blankly toward the fluttering skirts. Their mouths slowly fell open.
For one fleeting moment. They caught a glimpse of something that normally required a trip to a brothel to see.
Their minds went completely blank.
The next instant—
PFFT!
"Yak!"
"D-Dirt...!"
"I got dirt in my mouth!"

"I almost had a heart attack." One knight let out a helpless laugh.
Another guard smiled proudly.
"As expected of our Lord."
The maids also giggled among themselves, their earlier shock quickly turning into admiration.
"So beautiful."
"They’re shining."
Luke simply smiled at everyone’s reactions.
Then he bent his knees slightly.
His enormous silver wings slowly stretched to their full length.
Fwoooosh Power gathered beneath them.
The surrounding air visibly stirred.
Luke looked toward the distant sky.
"Let’s go."
BOOM!!
With a single powerful flap—
The gigantic wings unleashed a violent blast of wind.
Dust exploded outward.
Leaves danced wildly through the air.
The force alone sent powerful gusts sweeping across the courtyard.
"My skirt!"
"Kyaa!"
The nearby maids immediately cried out in surprise.
Their dresses fluttered violently in the sudden wind.
Blushing bright red.
They hurriedly grabbed their skirts with both hands before they could fly any higher.
Some squatted instinctively.
Others turned sideways to shield themselves.
"W-Wait...!"
"Hold it!"
Meanwhile.
"S-So white." A few young knights stared blankly toward the fluttering skirts.
Their mouths slowly fell open.
For one fleeting moment.
They caught a glimpse of something that normally required a trip to a brothel to see.
Their minds went completely blank.
The next instant—
PFFT!
"Yak!"
"D-Dirt...!"
"I got dirt in my mouth!"

chapters.title: Chapter 177: Serves You Right, Perverts!
paragraphs: Because they had been foolish enough to stare.
The dust and tiny pebbles kicked up by Luke’s takeoff flew straight into their wide-open mouths.
"Cough!"
"Ptui! Ptui!"
Several knights immediately bent over, desperately spitting out dirt.
One even rubbed his tongue with a disgusted expression.
"Ugh! It tastes awful!"
Seeing the pitiful scene.
The maids, who had finally managed to hold down their skirts, glared at them.
’Serves you right!’
’Perverts!’
One maid stomped her foot. Another covered her blushing face.
"Hmph!"
Without another word. They hurriedly ran back toward the servants quarters.
Their dresses, Hair. And even their faces were now covered with dust.
It would take quite a while before they looked presentable again.
High above Luke happened to glance downward. The scene immediately entered his eyes.
An embarrassed smile appeared on his face.
"Ahem!."
"Next time."
"I should probably take off from a stone courtyard."
"That way, maids won’t have to suffer skirt attack again and poor knights don’t have to eat dirt as well."
He scratched his cheek awkwardly before shaking his head.
Soon his attention shifted elsewhere.
The silver wings beat steadily against the wind as he soared even higher.
From this altitude...
The entire Blackstone Highlands spread out beneath him like a magnificent map.
The bustling marketplace immediately caught his attention.
Unlike the quiet streets from before. The town had become lively once again.
People walked from stall to stall. Children laughed as they chased one another through the streets.
Merchants loudly promoted their goods.
The aroma of freshly cooked food drifted upward.
Everywhere he looked. Life had returned to the territory.
Many citizens had even gathered together to celebrate.
Cheers echoed through the marketplace.
"Our Lord defeated a Mid-Golden Knight!"
"Haha! Tonight’s drinks are on me!
"Long live Baron Luke!"
Some taverns were already overflowing with customers.
Others had hung colorful banners outside their buildings.
The entire territory buzzed with excitement.
There were also mercenary companies escorting merchant caravans into the territory.
Seeing the growing flow of people. Luke recalled what Osric had reported earlier.
More and more Iron Knights had begun arriving in the Blackstone Highlands.
Even a handful of Bronze Knights had chosen to settle here.
Most of them belonged to adventurer parties or mercenary companies.
Of course, Joining the territory didn’t mean they had sworn loyalty to Luke.
Not yet.
Instead they had simply decided to make Blackstone their primary base of operations.
From now on they would spend most of their time here.
Accept quests here. Rest here. Purchase supplies here.
And naturally spend their earnings here as well.
In many ways that alone greatly benefited the territory.
More adventurers meant. More monsters being hunted. More bandits eliminated. More dangerous quests completed.
Many problems that would otherwise require the territory’s soldiers could now be solved through guild commissions.
Luke smiled faintly.
’As long as they obey the rules. They’re all welcome here.’
Then he also noticed the size of blackstone highlangs, as this was his first observing from the sky.
Because earlier, with the arcane sky tower. He didn’t done at that time.
The territory wasn’t particularly large. Roughly one kilometer in length and about eight hundred meters in width.
Even so its layout had been carefully planned.
The Lord’s Estate occupied the highest point.
Below it, Lay the bustling marketplace.
Further downhill rows of residential districts stretched across the slopes.
And beyond those the farmlands extended toward the lower plains.
Every morning the citizens had to walk down from the residential area before beginning their work in the fields.
It wasn’t the most convenient arrangement. But the mountain terrain left little choice.
With that thought. His gaze drifted toward several large buildings standing prominently within the town.
The Adventurers Guild.
The rhythmic sounds of weapons and lively conversations could be heard even from above.
Next...
The Blacksmith Guild.
Smoke continuously rose from its chimneys as the constant ringing of hammers echoed throughout the district.
Then came...
The Alchemist Association.
Its elegant building stood quietly, carrying a faint fragrance of herbs and potions.
Finally...
The Merchant Association.
The busiest building of them all.
Merchants entered and exited almost without pause.
Watching them from the sky...
Luke suddenly realized something.
All four organizations. Belonged to massive continent-wide organizations.
He had first encountered them back in Stormveil County.
At the time he had assumed they were only important in large cities.
Now, however he understood the truth.
Every noble territory possessed branches of these organizations.
Whether it was a barony, A viscounty. Or even a duchy. Their presence was almost universal.
The only difference was the scale.
Wealthier territories boasted grand headquarters with extensive facilities and hundreds of personnel.
Smaller territories, like Blackstone until recently. Only maintained modest branches capable of handling basic operations.
Then he also noticed. That Workers continuously carried construction materials inside.
Scaffolding had already been erected around several buildings.
Additional floors were being constructed. Walls were being expanded.
Even the surrounding courtyards were undergoing renovations.
Luke couldn’t help but chuckle.
"So."
"You’ve finally decided to invest in my territory?" His amused smile carried a hint of sarcasm.
When the Blackstone Highlands had struggled for survival. Not a single one of those organizations had offered meaningful assistance.
The territory had remained poor for years. Almost forgotten.
Yet now, the moment its future became bright. Everyone wanted a share of the benefits.
’How realistic.’ Luke smiled faintly. Businessmen truly followed profit.
Still his expression gradually became thoughtful.
Because he understood something else. The people belonging to those major organizations. Especially those from larger branches were notoriously proud.
He had personally experienced it back in Stormveil County.
Despite being the Hero. Most guild officials had treated him with only the minimum level of courtesy required by etiquette. Nothing more.
The only exception. Had been the manager of the Merchant Association.
That man had shown genuine respect from the very beginning.
Thinking back on it. Luke’s smile slowly faded.
"They haven’t even visited me once." He quietly muttered to himself.
If those organizations truly intended to deepen their investment in Blackstone. The proper courtesy would’ve been to meet the territory’s lord first.

chapters.title: Chapter 178: The Rising Watchtower
paragraphs: Yet none of them had done so.
Luke wasn’t angry. Merely curious. Then he recalled another detail.
Before the recent renovations. He was fairly certain there hadn’t been anyone stronger than a Silver-ranked official managing those branches.
"So that was the reason." Luke’s eyes flashed with understanding.
"No wonder for all these years."
"Hardly any bandits dared to openly attack the territory."
He folded his arms while quietly organizing the information in his mind.
"And Roland also never made a move either."
Everything finally clicked together. The four major organizations.
They still possessed four Silver-ranked experts.
If anyone recklessly provoked them. The consequences wouldn’t be pleasant.
Even Roland would’ve had to think twice before offending four continent-wide organizations simultaneously.
Luke slowly nodded. "Makes sense now."
Still his eyes narrowed.
"Business is business. They can renovate. They can expand."
"If they think they’ll quietly profit from my territory without paying anything."
A faint smile slowly spread across his lips. "Then they’re dreaming."
His smile became noticeably more cunning. "Free benefits are expensive in Blackstone."
"I’ll deal with them after I finish today’s work."
Giving the four headquarters one last glance. Luke beat his massive silver wings.
FWOOOSH!!
His figure instantly shot across the sky.
Only a short while later. The towering main gate of Blackstone came into view.
And also the surrounding defensive wall had already taken shape.
Hundreds of workers moved back and forth with remarkable efficiency.
Some transported massive stone blocks. Others mixed mortar.
His Earth mage also continuously reinforced the foundations.
Judging from the current pace. The walls would likely be completed within just a few more days.
"Faster than expected." Luke nodded in satisfaction.
Then he descended toward a spacious open area near the gate.
The giant silver wings folded slightly behind him.
THUD!!
His feet landed firmly on the ground. Which brings a wave of dust as its spread outward.
Fwoosh!
The sudden arrival immediately attracted everyone’s attention.
Passing merchants stopped their wagons. Adventurers lowered their mugs and looked over.
Even ordinary citizens paused what they were doing.
Children pointed excitedly toward the silver wings behind their lord.
"LORD!!!" Cheers erupted throughout the area.
"Our Lord!"
"Baron Luke!
"Long live Lord Luke!"
Smiles bloomed across every faces. Some workers immediately put down their tools.
Even several elderly citizens bowed respectfully toward him.
Their eyes were filled with gratitude.
After all ever since Luke had become the Lord of Blackstone. Their lives had changed dramatically.
Food was no longer scarce. Construction was happening everywhere.
The roads were being repaired. Gangs had disappeared.
And just yesterday their Lord had even defeated a Mid-Golden Knight.
To them Luke wasn’t merely their Baron anymore. He had become the hope of the Blackstone Highlands.
Watching everyone’s enthusiastic expressions. Luke smiled helplessly.
’Popularity has its own problems.’
Still he didn’t dislike it.
With a gentle flap his enormous silver wings slowly folded behind his back before disappearing into particles of silver light.
The crowd watched with amazement.
"So cool."
"I wish I could fly too."
Luke simply chuckled.
Then he reached into his Spatial Ring.
A rolled blueprint appeared in one hand. Which looked like magic scroll.
Of course they were merely props.
The real construction would be carried out by the system.
The scrolls existed only to provide a reasonable explanation in everyone else’s eyes.
Luke calmly looked toward the gathered crowd.
"Everyone step back." His gentle voice echoed.
And the citizens immediately obeyed.
"Move back!"
"Give Lord Luke some space!"
"Quick!"
The guards also stepped forward to maintain order.
Within moments a wide open area appeared before Luke.
Among the crowd an adventurer scratched his chin while staring at the scrolls.
"That’s an Earth Magic Scroll?" His eyes widened slightly.
"Baron Luke is sure wealthy. As those things cost a fortune."
The female adventurer standing beside him crossed her arms.
"I’m more curious about, what exactly is he planning to build?"
A nearby merchant nodded repeatedly.
"Knowing Baron Luke. It definitely won’t be something ordinary."
Because everyone already saw his earlier summoning of Warwalker fortress.
Which spread curiosity among the crowd. So everyone fixed their eyes on Luke.
Then Luke slowly unrolled the blueprint.
He gave it one final glance. "Let’s begin.
The next instant—
RIPPPP!!
The magic scroll tore apart in Luke’s hand. And a brilliant yellow radiance instantly erupted from within.
FWOOOOOM!!
The dazzling light swallowed the entire area. People instinctively covered their eyes.
"W-What is that?!"
"So bright!"
"My eyes!"
The ground beneath Luke suddenly began to tremble.
RUMBLE!! RUMBLE!!
"What-what’s happening?!"
"The ground is shaking!"
Several horses neighed in panic, while merchants hurriedly grabbed their reins.
The adventurers immediately became alert.
"Everyone, stay back!"
The guards shouted, escorting the citizens farther away.
Then the earth itself began to rise.
GRRRR!!
Huge chunks of dark stone erupted from underground.
One layer after another the huge structure rapidly assembled itself before everyone’s eyes.
Walls connected. Floors formed. Iron doors locked into place.
Blue runes carved themselves across the stone surface.
At the summit a gigantic mana crystal {Purest of Aether is Mana. same for mana crystal.} slowly emerged, pulsing with a gentle azure glow.
Hummmmm...
Within only a few moments a huge watchtower stood proudly before everyone.
It stood nearly 15 meters tall, equivalent to a five-story building.
Its circular base measured roughly 8 meters across.
The entire structure was built from reinforced enchanted dark-gray stone, giving it an imposing and sturdy appearance.
Faint blue magical runes glowed along every edge of the walls.
Narrow arrow slits lined the lower floors, while spacious observation windows overlooked the surroundings from the highest level.
The ground-floor entrance consisted of a large reinforced iron gate.
Above crenelated battlements surrounded a central mana crystal beacon, whose soft blue light rhythmically pulsed into the sky.
The detection runes embedded across the exterior quietly shimmered, giving the entire tower an otherwordly aura.
For a long moment nobody spoke.
The entire area fell deathly silent.
An elderly merchant’s walking cane slipped from his trembling hand.
Clack his mouth remained wide open.
Nearby adventurers stared upward in disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 179: The Sky Full of Titans
paragraphs: "H-How..."
"A watchtower."
"Instantly?"
One Bronze-ranked mercenary slowly swallowed.
"This-this isn’t ordinary Earth Magic."
As he had never witnessed construction on such a scale in his life.
The merchants were even more shocked. Their expressions completely changed.
Their merchant instincts immediately calculated its value.
’Such a tower.’
’How many months would it normally take to build?’
’How much would it cost?’
’Hundreds? No... thousands of gold coins.’
One merchant’s lips trembled.
Luke simply kept a calm smile.
He then turned toward the gate guards.
"You."
"Take your position."
"Yes, My Lord!"
One of the guards immediately saluted before rushing toward the tower.
Tap! Tap! Tap!
His footsteps echoed through the spiral staircase.
A few moments later. He appeared atop the battlements.
The guard looked around. Then his eyes widened. "Amazing."
He could see the trade road stretching far into the distance.
The nearby forests. The mountain paths.
Even approaching caravans that appeared as tiny dots on the horizon.
"My Lord!"
His excited voice echoed from above.
"The visibility is incredible!"
"I can monitor almost the entire eastern road!"
The nearby guards couldn’t help smiling proudly.
Meanwhile...
The citizens became even more excited.
"Wow!"
"We finally have a watchtower!"
"Our territory’s security just became much stronger!"
"If monsters come."
"We’ll know immediately!"
"And if bandits appear."
"The guards can prepare before they even reach us!"
Excited discussions spread throughout the crowd.
The merchants, however thought about something entirely different.
Especially those who had attended Luke’s meeting earlier.
A smile gradually spread across their faces.
"So Baron Luke wasn’t exaggerating."
"He really meant it.
"If one watchtower can appear instantly."
"Then the others won’t take long either."
Thinking about that their hearts became lighter.
Once the entire trade route was protected by these towers. Travel would become far safer.
However another thought quietly surfaced in everyone’s minds.
’Wait...’
’Exactly how many Earth Magic Scrolls does Baron Luke possess?’
Luke, naturally. Didn’t hear a single one of their thoughts.
His silver wings slowly unfolded once more.
This time he deliberately flapped them far more gently.
Fwoosh only a mild breeze spread across the surroundings.
With another smooth flap, he gracefully ascended into the sky.
Whoosh!
Soon he hovered high above the eastern road.
The newly completed watchtower gradually shrank beneath him.
Luke silently counted in his mind.
"One completed."
"But I still have, Nine hundred and ninety-nine Watchtower."
Stopping in midair he slowly turned around.
Behind him the entire Blackstone Highlands stood proudly upon the mountains.
Then he turned his face and silently looked toward the horizon.
From this altitude the geography of the Blackstone Highlands became much clearer.
The territory had been established near the eastern side of the Stormhowl Mountains.
More precisely along the lower mountain slopes that connected directly to the Human Kingdom.
To the north a single trade road stretched endlessly through the mountains.
It wound across cliffs, valleys, and narrow passes.
A road nearly one thousand kilometers long.
Blackstone itself was located roughly one hundred kilometers from its eastern entrance.
Although both the Human Kingdom and the neighboring races claimed the mountain ranges on their respective sides. The mountains themselves remained largely untouched.
As not a single city stood anywhere within the mountains forest of edges.
Only nature and countless magical beasts.
Luke quietly observed the magnificent landscape.
Then he slowly shook his head. "Enough sightseeing."
So with a thought he deactivated the first form of the Faceless Titan.
The majestic wings behind his back gradually dissolved.
For one brief moment. Luke simply floated in the sky.
Then—
Gravity reclaimed him.
WHOOSH!!
His body immediately began plummeting toward the earth.
The roaring wind exploded past his ears. His clothes fluttered violently.
The clouds above rapidly disappeared.
The mountains below rushed closer at astonishing speed.
He was falling from nearly, five thousand meters.
Any ordinary person would have already screamed in terror.
Luke merely smiled. His expression remained perfectly calm.
Then he quietly spoke.
"Nyx Ascension." The moment those words left his lips—
BOOOOOOM!!
An overwhelming wave of darkness erupted from his body.
The surrounding air visibly distorted.
Void energy burst outward like an endless black ocean.
The sunlight itself seemed to dim. The roaring wind suddenly fell silent.
As if even nature held its breath. Within the storm of darkness.
Luke’s body began to change. His physique rapidly expanded.
In only a heartbeat. He transformed into the Void Titan—Nyx.
Standing nearly fourteen feet tall.
His shoulder-length dark-blue hair danced gracefully in the violent air currents.
Then above his head. Space itself distorted.
A circle of absolute darkness slowly condensed. Void energy continuously flowed toward it.
Until—
A black halo silently formed.
Not made of light. But of condensed Void itself.
It floated serenely above his head. While rotating slowly.
The next instant. Luke raised his hand. Space beside him silently distorted.
Vmmmm.
"Valzareth." His calm voice echoed through the sky.
Immediately liquid-like black-blue energy surged from the void.
It wrapped around his gigantic body layer after layer.
Within only a heartbeat.
The towering Void Titan stood completely encased in the majestic Valzareth Armor.
The dark armor reflected faint azure light. While ancient runes pulsed softly across its surface.
Then he slowly spoke again.
"Shadow of Nyx." His quiet voice carried across the sky.
The space behind him suddenly rippled.
Ripple. Ripple. Ripple.
Ten separate distortions appeared one after another.
Then—
WHOOM!
One figure stepped out.
Then another.
And another.
Until...
Ten identical figures silently dropping behind him.
Every single one was the Void Titan Nyx. Every single one wore the complete Valzareth Armor.
Even the black halo floated above each of their heads.
From a distance it looked as though eleven Void beings had appeared simultaneously.
Luke looked back at them. A faint smile appeared beneath his helmet.
"Just as I thought."
The name of the skill was Shadow of Nyx.
Yet high above the grounds. There wasn’t a single shadow beneath him.
And still the dopplegängers had appeared without the slightest difficulty.
That confirmed his earlier suspicion.
The skill didn’t actually require shadows.

sentences.text: "H-How..."
"A watchtower."
"Instantly?"
One Bronze-ranked mercenary slowly swallowed.
"This-this isn’t ordinary Earth Magic."
As he had never witnessed construction on such a scale in his life.
The merchants were even more shocked.
Their expressions completely changed.
Their merchant instincts immediately calculated its value.
’Such a tower.’
’How many months would it normally take to build?’
’How much would it cost?’
’Hundreds?
No... thousands of gold coins.’
One merchant’s lips trembled.
Luke simply kept a calm smile.
He then turned toward the gate guards.
"You."
"Take your position."
"Yes, My Lord!"
One of the guards immediately saluted before rushing toward the tower.
Tap!
Tap!
Tap!

A few moments later.
He appeared atop the battlements.
The guard looked around.
Then his eyes widened.
"Amazing."

The nearby forests.
The mountain paths.
Even approaching caravans that appeared as tiny dots on the horizon.
"My Lord!"
His excited voice echoed from above.
"The visibility is incredible!"
"I can monitor almost the entire eastern road!"
The nearby guards couldn’t help smiling proudly.
Meanwhile...
The citizens became even more excited.
"Wow!"
"We finally have a watchtower!"
"Our territory’s security just became much stronger!"
"If monsters come."
"We’ll know immediately!"
"And if bandits appear."
"The guards can prepare before they even reach us!"
Excited discussions spread throughout the crowd.

Especially those who had attended Luke’s meeting earlier.
A smile gradually spread across their faces.
"So Baron Luke wasn’t exaggerating."
"He really meant it.
"If one watchtower can appear instantly."
"Then the others won’t take long either."
Thinking about that their hearts became lighter.
Once the entire trade route was protected by these towers.
Travel would become far safer.
However another thought quietly surfaced in everyone’s minds.
’Wait...’
’Exactly how many Earth Magic Scrolls does Baron Luke possess?’
Luke, naturally.
Didn’t hear a single one of their thoughts.
His silver wings slowly unfolded once more.
This time he deliberately flapped them far more gently.
Fwoosh only a mild breeze spread across the surroundings.
With another smooth flap, he gracefully ascended into the sky.
Whoosh!
Soon he hovered high above the eastern road.
The newly completed watchtower gradually shrank beneath him.
Luke silently counted in his mind.
"One completed."
"But I still have, Nine hundred and ninety-nine Watchtower."
Stopping in midair he slowly turned around.
Behind him the entire Blackstone Highlands stood proudly upon the mountains.
Then he turned his face and silently looked toward the horizon.
From this altitude the geography of the Blackstone Highlands became much clearer.
The territory had been established near the eastern side of the Stormhowl Mountains.
More precisely along the lower mountain slopes that connected directly to the Human Kingdom.
To the north a single trade road stretched endlessly through the mountains.
It wound across cliffs, valleys, and narrow passes.
A road nearly one thousand kilometers long.
Blackstone itself was located roughly one hundred kilometers from its eastern entrance.
Although both the Human Kingdom and the neighboring races claimed the mountain ranges on their respective sides.
The mountains themselves remained largely untouched.
As not a single city stood anywhere within the mountains forest of edges.
Only nature and countless magical beasts.
Luke quietly observed the magnificent landscape.
Then he slowly shook his head.
"Enough sightseeing."
So with a thought he deactivated the first form of the Faceless Titan.
The majestic wings behind his back gradually dissolved.
For one brief moment.
Luke simply floated in the sky.
Then—
Gravity reclaimed him.
WHOOSH!!
His body immediately began plummeting toward the earth.
The roaring wind exploded past his ears.
His clothes fluttered violently.
The clouds above rapidly disappeared.
The mountains below rushed closer at astonishing speed.
He was falling from nearly, five thousand meters.
Any ordinary person would have already screamed in terror.
Luke merely smiled.
His expression remained perfectly calm.

chapters.title: Chapter 180: The System’s Tease
paragraphs: The name was merely symbolic. Its true power had nothing to do with darkness cast by light.
Luke’s smile widened slightly.
"Excellent."
"That removes one of this ability’s greatest weaknesses."
Previously an intelligent opponent might have tried to eliminate every surrounding shadow.
If that had been the true condition for activating the skill.
The ability could have become nearly useless.
But now that concern completely disappeared.
Whether beneath the blazing sun. Above the endless clouds.
Or within a realm of pure light.
The Shadow of Nyx could still be summoned.
Then Luke slowly raised one armored hand.
"Go."
The very next moment. Their helmets materialized over their faces.
Clang!
Clang!
Clang!
Ten identical visors snapped shut almost in unison.
Then—
Blink.
One disappeared.
Then another.
Then all ten vanished simultaneously.
WHOOSH!
Only tiny ripples in space remained where they had stood.
Each dopplegänger instantly teleported 1km away, while maintaining a perfect distance balance to each other.
Watching them leave. Luke silently nodded.
Upon reaching the Bronze Knight Realm. The skill had evolved once again.
He could now maintain ten dopplegängers simultaneously.
And unlike before each one could remain active for nearly one full hour.
Of course that was only if Luke summoned all ten dopplegängers simultaneously.
The greater the number. The greater the strain on his stamina.
Once those were exhausted. Both the clones and his transformation would naturally be forced to end.
However if he maintained only one dopplegänger. The burden became dramatically lighter.
In that state he could remain transformed for a much longer period.
Luke silently calculated the difference.
Then he recalled another important point.
With his current 100% attribute amplification—
A complete one-times increase—
His Void Titan form already possessed the physical strength of a peak Bronze Knight genius.
Not just any Peak Bronze Knight. But a truly talented one.
After all knights weren’t all equal.
Across the continent. There were ordinary knights. Average knights. Talented knights.
And monsters who stood at the very peak of their generation.
Luke believed his current strength belonged to the third category.
A warrior who possessed an A-Rank Origin Skill. And had already reached Peak Bronze Knight.
Although he wasn’t completely certain yet.
"It’s only a rough estimate."
"I’ll have to verify it in an actual battle."
Still.
His confidence never wavered.
Even if an A-Rank genius truly stood before him.
Luke was certain of one thing.
He would win. And he would win quickly.
Not merely because of his raw strength.
But because his abilities were simply broken.
His gaze shifted toward the black-blue armor covering his body.
Valzareth.
As long as he possessed enough Aether. He could freely teleport up to one kilometer away.
Again.
And again.
And again.
Luke narrowed his glowing galactic eyes thoughtfully.
"Perhaps."
"That’s the reason it didn’t gain a new ability after crossing realm, like my titan form gave."
After all.
An armor capable of limitless teleportation with almost negligible Aether consumption was already powerful enough.
"Or." Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully while continuing to freefall through the sky.
"Maybe there’s another hidden condition?"
"Like the Arcane Sky Tower."
"Perhaps Valzareth also has an evolution requirement that hasn’t been fulfilled yet."
The thought lingered in his mind.
Just then—
[Kekeke. (¬‿¬)]
The System’s mischievous laughter suddenly echoed inside his head.
Luke’s eyebrow twitched.
He slowly looked at the floating screen.
"You know something, don’t you?"
A brief silence followed.
Then another window quietly popped up.
Luke stared at the shrugging emoji for several seconds.
His mouth twitched violently.
"Someone..."
"Please uninstall this emoji pack from my System."
He cursed inwardly.
The System, however didn’t respond.
It merely kept displaying the shrugging emoji as if proudly declaring—
"Figure it out yourself."
Luke couldn’t help rolling his eyes.
"One day."
"I’m seriously going to beat this System."
Far away the System silently snickered.
Meanwhile.
The ten dopplegängers acted simultaneously.
Almost as though they shared a single consciousness.
"Null Veil of Nyx."
Ten calm voices echoed across different corners of the sky.
Whoom.
Pitch-black Void energy instantly flowed around every clone. Dark mist coiled around their armored bodies.
Their presence rapidly faded. Sound disappeared. Aura vanished.
Even their existence seemed to blur.
Within moments the ten Void Titans became nearly impossible to detect.
The next instant—
"Void Step."
Blink!
One clone disappeared.
Blink!
A second vanished.
Then a third.
A fourth.
Until all ten silently teleported toward their assigned construction sites.
Across the eastern trade route. Dark ripples appeared one after another.
Each clone emerged atop cliffs. Beside forests. Near mountain passes. Or overlooking narrow sections of the road.
Without wasting a second. Every dopplegänger began scouting its surroundings.
Their glowing dark-blue eyes calmly swept across the landscape.
Soon the first clone stopped.
Several hundred meters away a group of nearly thirty bandits lounged around a crude campsite.
Some sharpened rusty swords. Others counted stolen coins.
One even laughed while drinking cheap ale.
The clone silently watched from atop a rocky cliff.
His emotionless gaze locked onto every single target.
Elsewhere...
The second clone also found something.
Hidden among the trees. Roughly fifty bandits had gathered around a campfire.
"Pass me the meat."
"Hahaha! After this we’ll rob another caravan!"
"Boss said tomorrow’s shipment will be huge!"
The smell of roasted meat drifted through the air.
Several bandits sat cross-legged, happily eating their lunch.
Completely unaware. That death had already arrived.
High above them...
The Void Titan stood silently beneath the cover of Null Veil of Nyx.
While the third dopplenger found two bandits, who were banging each forgot about this part.
So every other dopplegänger also completed its reconnaissance.
Within only a few minutes. Every clone had reported the same result.
Bandits.
Bandits everywhere.
Luke’s expression gradually darkened.
"So many."
Even after his earlier campaign a shocking number of bandit groups still remained within the forests surrounding Blackstone.
His original plan had been simple.
Build the watchtowers and while traveling between locations. Completely eliminate every remaining bandit nest along the trade route.
One task.
Two objectives.
Maximum efficiency.
Yet...
Even he hadn’t expected to find this many.
Luke narrowed his glowing eyes. "Why haven’t they fled?"

chapters.title: Chapter 181: Arrogance or Ignorance
paragraphs: Any sensible bandit should have abandoned the region after hearing the news.
After all.
The entire kingdom now knew that Baron Luke possessed Mid-Golden Knight combat power.
Remaining here was practically asking for death.
A thought soon crossed his mind.
"I see."
A cold smile appeared beneath his helmet.
"They probably assumed that I and the army were still in Windmarch Reach."
Returning from there would naturally require time.
That delay had likely given these bandits a false sense of security.
Luke slowly shook his head.
"Arrogance..."
He paused briefly.
"...Or ignorance."
Either way the outcome would be identical.
His gaze turned ice-cold. "Seems I have to paint the forest red once again."
At that moment.
Information continuously flowed back through the connection shared with his ten dopplegängers.
Every enemy position. Every patrol route. Every hidden camp.
Everything was transmitted directly into Luke’s mind.
A complete battlefield map formed almost instantly.
The corners of his lips lifted slightly. "Found you all."
He no longer hesitated. With a single thought. He issued the command.
"Do it."
Across ten different locations—
Excluding Luke’s original body—
Ten Void Titans moved simultaneously.
WHOOSH!!
Their figures blurred. Like shadows slipping through space. Before the bandits could even sense danger
Shhhk!
A faint sound. So soft that even the wind almost drowned it out.
The next instant. Every Iron Knight and Body Temper Realm bandit froze in place.
Several of them instinctively blinked.
One even frowned in confusion.
"What?"
Then their vision suddenly tilted.
The sky. The trees. The ground. Everything spun upside down.
Only then did they realize—
Their heads were no longer attached to their bodies.
Thud.
One severed head landed upon the soft forest floor.
Then another.
And another.
Within moments dozens of heads rolled across the dirt.
Thud.
Thud.
Roll.
Silence.
Utter silence.
No terrified screams. No cries for help. No desperate final words.
Only...
Chirp. Chirp.
The peaceful songs of birds echoed through the forest.
As if nature hadn’t noticed the massacre at all.
A heartbeat later—
FSSSHHH!!
Blood erupted from every headless corpse simultaneously.
Like crimson fountains.
The lifeless bodies swayed unsteadily before collapsing one after another.
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
Far From the battlefield.
Luke quietly observed everything through his shared vision.
Even he couldn’t help raising an eyebrow.
"Nyx’s speed." A faint smile appeared beneath his helmet. "Really is something."
Although he had spent thousands of hours training inside time chamber.
Most of that time had been devoted to mastering Caelith’s Titan Form.
Compared to it.
His experience using Nyx was surprisingly limited.
Yet after witnessing this battle. He finally understood something.
Nyx wasn’t merely powerful.
He was absurd.
Luke silently replayed the scene in his mind. "Interesting."
Then he recalled something Nyx had once told him.
The Faceless Titan—Myrkhal. Could only perfectly replicate Titan Forms possessing Greater Bloodlines.
Or anything below that level.
That was exactly what Nyx had explained back then.
He also had said one interesting thing.
"If Myrkhal is hiding other forms, then even we don’t know."
At the time Luke hadn’t understood what he meant.
But now he did.
"The real Titan Forms." He quietly muttered those words.
Nyx. Caelith. Myrkhal.
The real tittan, the source from which countless lower-bloodline Titans had descended.
Which also meant every aspect of them had reached its absolute peak.
Strength. Speed. Defense. Vitality. Control. Everything.
Far beyond any ordinary Titan possessing a Greater Bloodline or lower.
Luke slowly pieced together the realization.
"So that’s what he meant." A thoughtful smile appeared on his face.
Take the Void Titan—Nyx, for example.
His greatest authority undoubtedly lay in controlling the Void.
That was his true specialty.
However that didn’t mean the rest of his abilities were lacking.
On the contrary even in terms of pure physical strength.
Or raw movement speed.
Nyx could still overwhelm a lower-bloodline Titan whose entire specialty was strength or speed.
That realization had shocked Luke when Nyx first explained it.
Which suprised him.
As he rarely used Nyx for direct frontal combat.
Most of the time he transformed into Myrkhal, relying on its adaptability and available forms.
Because of that. he had never truly experienced what a True Titan was capable of physically.
Even The cosmic heart titan. He used cosmic system strength, rather than his own pysical strength.
But today’s battle, had changed that.
"Though even among the True Titans. Nyx’s speed should stand at the very peak."
After all unlike ordinary movement. He didn’t simply run.
He seemed to use the Void itself as a pathway.
Luke could vaguely sense it.
Only vaguely.
His current realm was still far too low to truly comprehend the mysteries of the Void.
It was like staring into an endless abyss through a tiny crack.
He could see that something incredible existed.
But not grasp it.
Not yet.
Luke slowly clenched his fist.
The Void energy around it rippled quietly.
"One day." A faint smile appeared beneath his helmet.
"I’ll understand the Void completely."
"And when that day comes."
His eyes shone with quiet determination, "I’ll finally witness the true power of Nyx."
After dealing with the bandits. Luke’s gaze swept across every campsite through the eyes of his dopplegängers.
Scattered everywhere were piles of stolen goods.
Wooden crates. Sacks of grain. Barrels of wine.
Weapons. Armor. Even bags filled with gold and silver coins.
It was obvious these had all been robbed from unfortunate caravans.
Then his turn his gaze toward far distance.
Several figures could be seen tied to nearby trees and wooden posts.
Some had bruises. Others looked pale from hunger.
A few had already lost all hope.
The moment the prisoners noticed the black-blue armored figure approaching.
Their bodies instinctively trembled.
"W-Who-" Before anyone could finish speaking.
Slash!
The ropes binding them were cleanly severed.
One after another the captives hurriedly freed themselves.
Luke’s calm voice soon followed.
"The bandits are dead."
"The road ahead is safe now."
He glanced toward the piles of supplies.
"Take whatever belongs to you."
"If there are items without owners. You may divide them among yourselves."
